BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p592/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p592/r4.speaker: عمر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p592/r4.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits ʿUmar’s counsel that the caliph safeguard the rights of the early Emigrants and accept the good of the Helpers who settled in the abode and faith before the Prophet’s migration, forgiving their faults.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p592/r4.anchor: أخرج عن عمر رضى الله عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r5.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates the settled Anṣār with Emigrants, making both groups recipients; another reading starts a sentence with يحبون as predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: والذين تبوؤا معطوف على المهاجرين، وهم الأنصار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r6.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī coordinates abode and faith as clauses: they settled in Medina and believed sincerely; other parses make تبوؤا imply adherence or faith a figurative dwelling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r6.anchor: فقيل: هو من عطف الجمل، أي واعتقدوا الإيمان وأخلصوا فيه، قاله أبو علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains دار الإيمان as the House of Faith or a name for Medina where emigration and faith appeared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أو أراد دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says they settled in the abode together with faith, making “before them” coherent; من قبلهم means before migration and حاجة means envy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p142/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والمعنى تبوؤا الدار مع الإيمان معا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r1.claim: The verse points to an Anṣārī who hosted the Prophet’s guest despite having only food for his children; the Prophet said God marveled at their action the previous night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r1.anchor: قصة الأنصاري مع ضيف الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، حيث لم يكن لهم إلا ما يأكل الصبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r2.claim: خصاصة means poverty, likened to gaps between a house’s sticks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r2.anchor: والخصاصة: الفاقة، مأخوذة من خصاص البيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r3.claim: Shuḥḥ is innate tightness about one’s possessions and eagerness to withhold; Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with kasra, unlike the majority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r3.anchor: والشح: اللؤم، وهو كزازة النفس على ما عندها، والحرص على المنع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r4.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r4.claim: A poetic line pictures a miserly soul resisting generosity; the verse about souls being brought face to face with stinginess is also linked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r4.anchor: يمارس نفسا بين جنبيه كزة ... إذا هم بالمعروف قالت له مهلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r5.claim: A report says paying required alms, hosting guests, and giving in hardship frees one from stinginess.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p143/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث: «من أدى الزكاة المفروضة وقرى الضيف وأعطى في النائبة فقد برىء من الشح»

NAHHAS:v4p396/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r5.claim: الذين can be genitive after the preposition, or nominative as the subject whose predicate is يحبون; in the genitive parse, يحبون is circumstantial or detached.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r5.anchor: الذين في موضع خفض أي للذين ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع بالابتداء

NAHHAS:v4p396/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r6.claim: هاجر إليهم means moved to them.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r6.anchor: أي انتقل إليهم وإذا كان الذين في موضع خفض كان يحبون في موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v4p396/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r7.claim: The clause is coordinated with يحبون.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r7.anchor: معطوف عليه وكذا ( ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة )

NAHHAS:v4p396/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r8.claim: They prefer the emigrants even when they themselves are in need of what they give away.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r8.anchor: أي فاقة إلى ما آثروا به

NAHHAS:v4p396/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r9.claim: خصاصة means need or a gap; any opening or hole in a wall is also called خصاصة.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r9.anchor: وكل كوة أو خلل في حائط فهو خصاصة

NAHHAS:v4p396/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r10.claim: يوق is jussive in the conditional, so its final alif is deleted; Basrans forbid retaining it, while Kufans permit it.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r10.anchor: جزم بالشرط فلذلك حذفت الألف منه ولا يجوز إثباتها إذا كان شرطا عند البصريين ويجوز عند الكوفيين

NAHHAS:v4p396/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r11.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v4p396/r11.claim: The Kufans cite the poetic ألم يأتيك despite the difference that alif never moves while ياء and واو can move; al-Nahhas says they conflated the long vowels and extended poetic license to Qur'anic readings.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r11.anchor: وشبهوه بقول الشاعر ( ألم يأتيك والأنباء تنمي ) والفرق بين ذا والأول

NAHHAS:v4p396/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r12.speaker: حمزة
NAHHAS:v4p396/r12.claim: The Kufans also apply this analysis to Hamza's reading لا تخف دركا ولا تخشى.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r12.anchor: وحملوا قراءة حمزة / لا تخف دركا ولا تخشى / عليه في أحد أقوالهم

NAHHAS:v4p396/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r13.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v4p396/r13.claim: Exegetes explain شح as taking wealth without right.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r13.anchor: وأهل التفسير على أن الشح أخذ المال بغير الحق

NAHHAS:v4p396/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r14.claim: In Arabic, شح is stronger than بخل: it describes extreme miserliness and withholding surplus wealth.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r14.anchor: والمعروف في كلام العرب أن الشح أزيد من البخل وأنه يقال شح فلان يشح إذا اشتد بخله ومنع فضل المال

NAHHAS:v4p396/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p396/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p396/r15.claim: An anonymous poetic line illustrates the miserly sense in الشحيح.
NAHHAS:v4p396/r15.anchor: كما قال ( ترى اللحز الشحيح إذا أمرت … عليه لماله فيها مهينا )

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r1.claim: One parse coordinates الذين with الفقراء as a genitive single-word coordination, with يحبون as a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r1.anchor: أنه عطف على الفقراء، فيكون مجرورا، ويكون من عطف المفردات، ويكون " يحبون " حالا

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r2.claim: Alternatively الذين is a subject whose predicate is يحبون, making it coordination of clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r2.anchor: أن يكون مبتدأ، خبره " يحبون " ، ويكون حينئذ من عطف الجمل

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r3.claim: One analysis gives تبوؤوا the sense of adhering to, allowing coordination with faith, which cannot literally be inhabited.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r3.anchor: ضمن " تبوؤوا " معنى لزموا، فيصح عطف الإيمان عليه؛ إذ الإيمان لا يتبوأ

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r4.claim: Another analysis supplies an omitted verb such as اعتقدوا, ألفوا, or أحبوا to govern الإيمان.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r4.anchor: أنه منصوب بمقدر، أي: واعتقدوا، أو وألفوا، أو وأحبوا

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r5.claim: A figurative analysis treats faith as a place surrounding and firmly intermingled with them, though it combines literal and figurative senses in one word, a disputed construction.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r5.anchor: فيجعل لاختلاطه بهم وثباتهم عليه كالمكان المحيط بهم، فكأنهم نزلوه

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers two city-name parses: دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان with ellipsis and substitution, or naming Medina الإيمان because it is the home of migration and the place where faith appeared.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r6.anchor: قال هذين الوجهين الزمخشري، وليس فيه إلا قيام أل مقام المضاف إليه

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r7.claim: Al-Samin questions whether the definite article can replace a genitive complement; the disputed issue is whether it can replace an attached pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r7.anchor: وهو محل نظر، وإنما يعرف الخلاف: هل تقوم أل مقام الضمير المضاف إليه

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r8.claim: Kufans allow the article to stand for a genitive pronoun, while Basrans reject that and posit an omitted pronoun in 79:39.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r8.anchor: الكوفيون يجيزونه كقوله تعالى: فإن الجنة هي المأوى

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya parses الإيمان as a comitative object, with it joined alongside the city; this pairing supports من قبلهم.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r9.anchor: السادس: أنه مصنوب على المفعول معه، أي: مع الإيمان معا، قاله ابن عطية

SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r10.claim: The comitative analysis is tested against the rule that its noun must also permit coordination; the example فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم instead requires an implicit verb.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9/r10.anchor: من باب إضمار الفعل لأنه لا يقال: أجمعت شركائي إنما يقال جمعت

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes حاجة as the thing needed, meaning the later Ansar do not desire anything the migrants received; the first pronoun is the Ansar and the second the migrants.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r1.anchor: أن الحاجة هنا على بابها من الاحتياج، إلا أنها واقعة موقع المحتاج إليه

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r2.claim: Another view takes حاجة to mean envy, with the pronouns assigned as in the preceding analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r2.anchor: أن الحاجة هنا من الحسد، قاله بعضهم، والضميران على ما تقدم قبل

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies an omitted مضاف before حاجة; on this parse both pronouns refer to those who settled the abode and faith.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: مس حاجة، أي: إنه حذف المضاف للعلم به

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r4.claim: The واو in ولو كان بهم is circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r4.anchor: قوله: { ولو كان بهم } واو الحال وقد تقدم الكلام عليها

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r5.claim: خصاصة means need; it comes from the gaps in a house, borrowed for poverty as a state interrupted by lack.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#2/r5.anchor: والخصاصة: الحاجة، وأصلها من خصاص البيت، وهي فروجه

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r1.claim: The common reading has يوق with quiescent waw and light qaf; Ibn Abi Abla and Abu Haywa read open waw with geminated qaf.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r1.anchor: العامة على سكون الواو وتخفيف القاف من الوقاية. وابن أبي عبلة وأبو حيوة بفتح الواو وشد القاف

SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r2.claim: The common reading has damma on شح; Ibn Abi Abla and Ibn Umar read kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:59:9#3/r2.anchor: والعامة بضم الشين من " شح " وابن أبي عبلة وابن عمر بكسرها

ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r1.claim: Those who settled in the abode and faith before the emigrants are the Helpers (Ansar).
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r1.anchor: (9) يعني الأنصار. (والإيمان من قبلهم) يعني المهاجرين.

ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r2.claim: The phrase “and faith before them” refers to the emigrants.
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r2.anchor: (والإيمان من قبلهم) يعني المهاجرين. (يحبون من هاجر إليهم)

ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r3.claim: The Helpers love the believers who emigrated to them.
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r3.anchor: (يحبون من هاجر إليهم) أي يحب الأنصار المؤمنين. (ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا).

ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r4.claim: The Helpers feel no resentment over what is given to the emigrants.
ZAJJAJ:v5p145#2/r4.anchor: (ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا). أي لا يجد الأنصار في صدورهم حاجة مما يعطى المهاجرون.

ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r1.claim: The believers who settled in the realm of faith love those seeking refuge and bear no resentment over what the newcomers receive.
ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r1.anchor: love all that come to them in search of refuge, and who harbour in their hearts no grudge for whatever the others may have been given

ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r2.claim: They give refugees preference even when they themselves are poor; those saved from covetousness attain happiness.
ASAD-NOTES:59:9/r2.anchor: give them preference over themselves, even though poverty be their own lot

ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n12/r1.claim: The earlier settlers preceded those who left the domain of evil, as explained in the following note.
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n12/r1.anchor: before the coming to them of

ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r1.claim: Historically these are Medina's Ansar, who embraced Islam before the Prophet and Meccan followers arrived, then shared homes and possessions generously with the refugees.
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r1.anchor: of Medina, who had embraced Islam

ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r2.claim: More broadly, this describes believers in every age living securely in Islam who welcome those forced to leave home to follow their faith.
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n13/r2.anchor: all true believers, at all times, who live in freedom and security within the realm of Islam

ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n14/r1.claim: Greed, niggardliness and covetousness are chief barriers to happiness in this life and the hereafter; compare surah 102.
ASAD-NOTES:59:9#n14/r1.anchor: greed, niggardliness and covetousness are pointed out here as the main obstacles to man's attaining to a happy state in this world and in the hereafter

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:r-124/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:r-124/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:r-124/r2.claim: In تبوؤوا الدار والإيمان, settling applies to the abode but not faith, so coordination implies a different omitted governing verb for faith, as in the saying about drinking milk and eating dates.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:r-124/r2.anchor: الإيمان لا يتبؤأ إنما يتبوأ الدار فهنا عطف على الدار لكن ليس بنفس المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p581/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p581/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p581/r1.claim: Coordination can join terms requiring different verbs: one settles in the home, not faith; in Yunus one gathers a plan and assembles partners. An omitted verb is understood, as in the Arab phrase “milk for drinking and dates for eating.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p581/r1.anchor: الإيمان لا يتبؤأ إنما يتبوأ الدار فهنا عطف

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p237/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p237/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p237/r5.claim: Verses 5–10 form a parenthetical digression answering objections about the Banū Naḍīr incident raised by Jews and hypocrites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p237/r5.anchor: In a parenthetical sentence, certain objections raised by the Jews and

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r1.claim: The incident should teach that God's and His Prophet's enemies were humiliated and God's faction prevailed; those still wishing to befriend them should consider the consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r1.anchor: how clearly God’s faction prevailed over Satan’s faction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r4.claim: The discussion of verses 5–10 is a parenthetical digression from the main topic, addressing Jewish and hypocrite objections to the Banū Naḍīr episode.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p242/r4.anchor: In this section, which forms a parenthetical sentence and is a digression from the main topic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p243/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p243/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p243/r4.claim: Islahi praises the Anṣār and early Muhājirūn for generosity toward immigrant brothers, preferring their needs over their own; this sacrifice and contentment befit believers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p243/r4.anchor: the Anṣār and the early Muhājirūn are praised for their sacrifice and contentment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r4.claim: The verse praises the Anṣār and earliest Muhājirūn for welcoming later immigrants without resentment or envy over their share in wealth and fay, and for preferring them despite their own needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r4.anchor: they do not feel any resentment that the immigrants have come over to them in multitudes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r5.claim: The coordinated expression suppresses a verb suited to its second object; the omission is recoverable from contextual indications, as in the Arabic analogies cited.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p249/r5.anchor: a verb which is appropriate for the second object is suppressed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r1.claim: As an example of the omitted verb, Islahi proposes ḥakkamū, yielding the sense that these people already had homes and had firmly rooted their faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r1.anchor: those who already have a place of residence and have also firmly rooted their faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r2.claim: The phrase primarily includes the Anṣār, but Islahi also includes the earliest Muhājirūn already settled in Madīnah with livelihoods: together they preceded later migrants in residence and faith, while the Anṣār alone preceded them only in having homes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r2.anchor: both of them are collectively ahead of the later ones

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r3.claim: They affectionately welcomed the many new arrivals and accepted that fay wealth would go to them or be shared with them, contentedly placing the newcomers' needs first.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r3.anchor: they are giving preference to their needs over their own

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r4.claim: Praising their altruism teaches believers to show mutual sympathy and generosity, while implicitly shaming hypocrites who demanded that Banū Naḍīr's remaining wealth be distributed as war spoils.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r4.anchor: the believers should be sympathetic, generous and altruistic to each other

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r5.claim: Shuḥ means greed and avarice; as a craving of the soul it is dangerous, and failure to master it can ruin one's Hereafter. Islahi renders it “selfishness” to stress this danger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r5.anchor: it becomes evident that it is one of the cravings found in it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r6.claim: Islahi warns that the hypocrites suffer from this spiritual disease and, unless they reform, will be doomed eternally.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p250/r6.anchor: This section of verses tells the hypocrites that they are inflicted with this malady

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r1.claim: Islahi cites a narration that selfish greed destroyed earlier nations by driving them to tyranny, sin and defiance, and severing kinship ties.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r1.anchor: It induced them to tyranny and they became tyrannical

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r2.speaker: exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r2.claim: The exegetes take the verse to add the Anṣār to the beneficiaries of fay, just as the preceding verses assign a share to the Muhājirūn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r2.anchor: Our exegetes are of the opinion that just as the previous verses state that the Muhājirūn also have a share in the wealth of fay

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r3.claim: Islahi rejects that reading: the Muhājirūn were mentioned because their needs strained the government, whereas no one disputed the Anṣār's share, and the previously named poor already included needy Anṣār.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r3.anchor: I am unable to understand this

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r4.claim: The verse instead says that the Anṣār and early Muhājirūn did not view incoming brothers as a financial threat: they welcomed them affectionately and stood ready to sacrifice, exemplifying the mutual care faith requires of every Muslim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p251/r4.anchor: they, in fact, welcome them with affection

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p252/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p252/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p252/r3.claim: The earlier warning about selfishness contrasts with the truthful, righteous people, who are entirely free of that spiritual disease.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p252/r3.anchor: in contrast, these truthful and righteous people are absolutely devoid of such maladies

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r1.claim: Most commentators take the clause as coordinated with the emigrants; it refers to the Helpers (Ansar).
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r1.anchor: الأكثرون على أنه معطوف على المهاجرين والمراد بهم الأنصار

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r2.claim: Tabawwu means settling in a place; al-mabāʾa is a dwelling place.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r2.anchor: والتبوؤ النزول في المكان ومنه المباءة للمنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r3.claim: The abode is Medina, and defining it as the abode honors it as the true abode God prepared for the Helpers.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r4.claim: The preferred construction metaphorically makes faith a settled homeland, using an implicit metaphor and its figurative completion.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r4.anchor: فباعتبار جعله مستقرا ومتوطنا على سبيل الاستعارة المكنية التخييلية

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r5.claim: Another construction uses a poetic pattern: they settled in the abode and made faith sincere.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r5.anchor: علفتها تبنا وماءا باردا + أيتبوأو الدار

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r6.claim: A further explanation treats settling as a metonym for its necessary consequence, staying in the abode and faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r6.anchor: التبوؤ مجاز مرسل عن اللزوم وهو لازم معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r7.claim: Another parsing supplies abode before faith, yielding the abode of migration and the abode of faith; al-Alusi finds this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r7.anchor: حذف مضاف أي ودار الإيمان فكأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r8.claim: The suggestion that الإيمان itself metaphorically means Medina, as the place where faith appears, is dismissed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r8.anchor: إن الإيمان مجاز عن المدينة سمي محل ظهور الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r9.claim: Taking the conjunction to mean together with their faith is also rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r9.anchor: الواو للمعية والمراد تبوأوا الدار مع إيمانهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r10.claim: Al-Dār is a conventional name for Medina, alongside al-Madīna, Ṭayba, Ṭāba, Yathrib, and Jābira.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r10.anchor: علم بالغلبة على المدينة كالمدينة وأنه أحد أسماء لها منها طيبة وطابة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r11.claim: Before them means before the emigrants and attaches to تبوؤوا, with an implicit reference to their migration.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r11.anchor: أي من قبل المهاجرين والجار متعلق بتبوأوا

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r12.claim: This wording need not claim that the Helpers believed before the emigrants, only that their faith was already firmly established and undisputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r12.anchor: ولا يلزم منه سبق إيمانهم ليقال : إن الأمر بالعكس

ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r13.claim: A permissible refinement is that the Helpers preceded the emigrants in being settled in faith, since they did not contest it when the emigrants displayed theirs.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p51#2/r13.anchor: ليس المراد سبق الأنصار لهم في أصل الإيمان بل

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r1.claim: A reversed-order reading makes the Helpers precede the emigrants only in settling the abode; al-Alusi rejects it as contrary to the apparent order and lacking a subtle rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r1.anchor: الكلام على التقديم والتأخير والتقدير تبوأوا الدار

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r2.claim: Another view says the verse establishes only that the Helpers’ combined settlement and faith preceded the emigrants’; the author disputes that one earlier component suffices.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r2.anchor: ما تدل الآية عليه تقدممجموع تبويء الأنصاري وإيمانهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r3.claim: The clause may be a circumstantial description of the Helpers or a new sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r3.anchor: إليهم ( في موضع الحالمن الموصول وقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r4.claim: One explanation treats their love as a figure for supporting emigrants without resentment or weariness when they need help.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r4.anchor: والكلام قيل : كناية عن مواساتهم المهاجرين

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r5.claim: Literally, they love emigrants because they migrated to them, out of love for faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r5.anchor: لحبهم الإيمان ( ولا يجدون في صدورهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r6.claim: They feel no desire for any portion of the spoils or other goods given to the emigrants; their souls do not covet it.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r6.anchor: ما أعطى المهاجرون ولم تطمع إلى شيء منه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r7.claim: Here حاجة means something one needs; وجد denotes practical awareness, and locating it in the chest is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r7.anchor: فالوجدان إدراك عملي وكونه في الصدر من باب المجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r8.claim: من may be partitive, explanatory with an omitted noun, or causal; the deleted noun طلب explains why the need never entered their minds.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r8.anchor: تبعيضية وجوز كونها بيانية والكلام على حذف مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes حاجة as resentment, anger, envy, or covetousness caused by the emigrants’ allotments; al-Alusi prefers the preceding explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52/r9.anchor: ولا يجدون في صدورهم ( أي ولا يعلمون في أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r1.claim: The object of يؤثرون need not be restricted to the emigrants; the phrase may mean preferring them in everything.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r1.anchor: لا يعتبر مفعول يؤثرون خصوص المهاجرين

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r2.claim: خصاصة is need or poverty, named from the gaps and openings left between the slats of a house.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r2.anchor: حاجة من خصاص البيت وهو ما يبقى بين عيدانهمن الفرج والفتوح

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi defines شح as meanness and a tight, avid soul inclined to withhold, citing a poetic line; it is innate, while bukhl is withholding one’s own wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r4.anchor: وهو أن تكون النفس كزة حريصة على المنع

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines شح as stinginess combined with habitual greed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r5.anchor: الشح بخل مع حرص وذلك فيما كان عادة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r6.claim: Hasan distinguishes bukhl as withholding what one possesses and شح as coveting what others possess.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r6.anchor: والشح أن يشح على ما في يدي الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r7.claim: When a man feared he was doomed because he was miserly, Ibn Masud said this was bukhl, not the verse’s شح; that شح is consuming another’s wealth unjustly.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنرجلا قال له : إني أخاف

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r8.claim: Ibn Umar says merely withholding one’s own wealth is bukhl; شح is desiring what one does not own.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r9.claim: Al-Alusi finds no lexicographic support for those reports as formal definitions, but understands شح as extreme greed that resents others’ generosity, consumes their wealth, or covets what is not one’s own.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r9.anchor: لم أر لأحد من اللغويين شيئا من هذه التفاسير للشح

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r10.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r10.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi Abla read يُوقَ with a doubled qaf.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبيعبلة ( ومن يوق ) بشد القاف

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r11.speaker: ابن عمر وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r11.claim: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abi Abla read شح with kasra on the shin; the readings have the same meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عمر وابن أبيعبلة ( شح ) بكسر الشين

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r12.claim: Being protected from the self’s greed comes through God’s enabling help, so one resists its dominant love of wealth and dislike of spending.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r12.anchor: ومعنى الآية ومنيوق بتوفيق الله تعالى ومعونته شحنفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r13.claim: The Helpers put emigrants before themselves in every kind of good thing, even arranging a guest’s food while their household went without.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r13.anchor: أكرمي ضيف رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a hungry visitor came to the Prophet, who sought a host; an Ansari, Abu Talha in one version, fed him while his family went without, and the Prophet said God marveled at them.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r14.anchor: يا رسول الله أصابني الجهد فأرسل إلى نسائه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r15.claim: Ibn Umar reports a sheep’s head passed among seven Companions’ households, each preferring the next, until it returned to the first; the verse was revealed about them.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p52#2/r15.anchor: تداوله أهل سبعة أبيات حتى رجع إلى الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r1.claim: The successful are those who attain every desired good and escape every harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r1.anchor: الفائزون بكل مطلوب الناجون من كلمكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r2.claim: The conditional conclusion is a fitting summation and praise, primarily encompassing the Helpers; singular من followed by plural أولئك tracks form then meaning and suggests few attain it in number but great stature.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r2.anchor: والجملة الشرطية تذييل حسن ومدح للأنصار بما هو غاية

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r3.anchor: ويفهم من الآية ذم الشح جدا وقد وردت أخبار كثيرة بذمه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r4.claim: A report from Anas says nothing has destroyed Islam as thoroughly as greed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r4.anchor: عن أنس مرفوعا ما محق الإسلام محق الشح قط

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits that faith and greed never coexist in a servant’s heart, nor do the dust of God’s path and Hellfire’s smoke; the collector graded it sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r5.anchor: عن أبيهريرة مرفوعا لا يجتمع غبار في سبيل الله

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r6.claim: The Prophet says that stinginess and bad character do not coexist in a Muslim; al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r6.anchor: عن أبيسعيد الخدري مرفوعا خصلتانلا يجتمعان

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r7.claim: Anas reports that God created Eden and its trees, which answered ‘The believers have succeeded’; God vowed that no miser would dwell there, and the Prophet recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r8.claim: The Prophet commands avoiding injustice and greed, saying greed destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and violating sacred limits.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r8.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أن رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : اتقوا الظلم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r9.claim: Protection from greed does not require giving away everything: paying zakat, hosting guests, and meeting hardship count as freedom from greed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r9.anchor: ينبغي أنيعلم أن تقوي الشح لا تتوقف على أن يكون الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن مجمع بن يحيى
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r10.claim: The Prophet says the person who pays zakat, hosts a guest, and gives in times of hardship is free of greed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r10.anchor: عن مجمع بن يحيى مرفوعا بريء من الشح من أدى الزكاة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r11.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله وأنس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r11.claim: Al-Alusi notes comparable reports from Jabir and Anas on being free of greed through such conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله ما يقرب منه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r12.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r12.claim: Ali says that whoever pays zakat on his wealth has been protected from greed.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p53/r12.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : من أدى زكاة ماله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says inner speech means the combined mental wording and meaning, which remains in the mind and is indicated by spoken expressions; Imam al-Ḥaramayn states this explicitly.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r1.anchor: بل المراد به مجموع اللفظ النفسي والمعنى وهو الذي يدور في الخلد وتدل عليه العبارات كما صرح به إمام الحرمين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r2.claim: In the example ‘Zayd is standing,’ beyond the four items listed by the objector is a fifth: the sentence as it exists mentally in imagined words indicating inward meanings; this is inner speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r2.anchor: أربعة أشياء كما ذكر المعترض وشيء خامس تركه وهو المراد وهي هذه الجملة بشرط وجودها في الذهن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r3.claim: The first objection fails because the opponents do include the combined mental word and meaning; speech is then composed of letters, inward and unseen in God and imagined in creatures.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r3.anchor: فحيث كان لا مخالفة لأن الكلام حينئذ مركب من الحروف إلا أنها نفسية غيبية في الحق خيالية في الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r5.claim: The third objection confuses God’s single attribute of being a speaker with speech addressed by Him: the latter is not one, since al-Ibāna divides it eternally into report, command, and prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r5.anchor: بل نص في الإبانة على إنقسامه إلى الخبر والأمر والنهي في الأزل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r6.speaker: نجم سليمان الطوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r6.claim: Al-Ṭūfī argues that uttered expression is literal speech and inner meaning figurative: listeners immediately understand the expression, and expressions alone actually affect hearers, while mental meanings affect potentially.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r6.anchor: وقال النجم سليمان الطوفي : إنما كان الكلام حقيقة في العبارة مجازا في مدلولها لوجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r7.speaker: المخالفون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r7.claim: The opponents say that Arabic uses ‘speech’ for both inner speech and uttered expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r7.anchor: وقال المخالفون : أستعمل لغة في النفسي والعبارة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects al-Ṭūfī’s inference from common immediate understanding: verbal use is frequent because it is needed, not because it alone is the word’s proper sense; usage for inner speech also supports literalness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r8.anchor: إنما هو لكثرة إستعماله في اللفظي لمسيس الحاجة إليه لا لكونه الموضوع له خاصة بدليل إستعماله لغة وعرفا في النفسي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r11.claim: Al-Ṭūfī says al-Akhtal’s famous line reads ‘bayān,’ not ‘speech’; if it reads ‘speech,’ he takes it figuratively for the thoughts enabling speech, and calls it poetic hyperbole favoring heart over tongue.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r11.anchor: وأما بيت الأخطل فالمشهور أن البيان وبتقدير أن يكون الكلام فهو مجاز عن مادته وهو التصورات المصححة له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī begins his rebuttal by arguing that frequent use does not establish exclusive denotation: ‘speech’ is used in language and convention for inner speech as well as utterance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p14/r12.anchor: بدليل إستعماله لغة وعرفا في النفسي والأصل في الإطلاق الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī denies lexical homonymy but argues for a shared conceptual meaning: grammarians define speech as what is spoken, whether little or much, literally or conventionally.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r1.anchor: ونحن لا ندعيه وإنما ندعي الإشتراك المعنوي وذلك أن الكلام في اللغة بنقل النحويين ما يتكلم به قليلا كان أو كثيرا حقيقة أو حكما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r2.claim: Against al-Ṭūfī’s claim that expressions alone affect hearers, Al-Ālūsī says meaningless words have no effect, while recalled words can affect someone without sound or letters; imagined mental words can therefore affect the psyche.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r2.anchor: إذا سمع كلاما لا يفهم معناه لا تؤثر ألفاظه في نفسه شيئا وقد يتذكر الإنسان في حالة سروه كلاما يحزنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the common reading ‘bayān’ in al-Akhtal’s line can mean either what clarifies, equivalent to speech, or clarification itself; the latter entails inner speech as the heart orders mental words for verbal expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r6.anchor: لأنه إما أسم مصدر بمعنى ما يبين به أو مصدر بمعنى التبيين وعلى الأول هو بمعنى الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Ṭūfī’s alternative—if the poem says ‘speech,’ it is figurative—concedes inner speech without realizing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r7.anchor: فلأن قوله وبتقدير أن يكون إلخ إقرار بالكلام النفسي من غير شعور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects calling the poem figurative as arbitrary because the default in an unqualified expression is literal meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r8.anchor: فلأن دعوى المجاز تحكم مع كون الأصل في الإطلاق الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that al-Akhtal merely exaggerates: he calls the line a factual insight and supports it with a report from Abū Saʿīd that eyes guide, ears funnel, and the tongue interprets.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p15/r9.anchor: بل هو تحقيق من غير مبالغة كما يفهم مما سلف فما ذكره هذا الشاعر كلمة حكمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r1.claim: These are the Helpers, who settled in Medina, making it their home of migration and faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r1.anchor: والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان} الأنصار تبوؤا الدار توطنوا الدار، أي: المدينة اتخذوها دار الهجرة والإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r2.claim: They accepted Islam in their own homes and built mosques two years before the Prophet arrived.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r2.anchor: من قبلهم} أي أسلموا في ديارهم وآثروا الإيمان وابتنوا المساجد قبل قدوم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسنتين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r3.claim: The construction means they settled in the home before the emigrants arrived; faith itself is not a place one inhabits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r3.anchor: والذين تبوؤا الدار من قبلهم أي من قبل قدوم المهاجرين عليهم، وقد آمنوا لأن الإيمان ليس بمكان تبوء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r4.claim: They felt no resentment, anger, or envy at what the emigrants received: the Prophet gave Banu Nadir’s property to the emigrants and none to the Helpers, who accepted this gladly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r4.anchor: حزازة وغيظا وحسدا {مما أوتوا} أي مما أعطى المهاجرين دونهم من الفيء، وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم أموال بني النضير بين المهاجرين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r5.claim: They preferred their emigrant brothers, giving them their own wealth and homes ahead of themselves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r5.anchor: أي يؤثرون على إخوانهم من المهاجرين بأموالهم ومنازلهم على أنفسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r6.claim: “Khaṣāṣah” means poverty and need; the Helpers divided their homes and property despite their own need.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r6.anchor: فاقة وحاجة إلى ما يؤثرون، وذلك أنهم قاسموهم ديارهم وأموالهم:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports an Ansari couple hosting a guest when they had only the children’s food: they feigned eating, let the children sleep hungry, and the Prophet said God admired their act; the verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p76/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاستضافه فبعث إلى نسائه هل عندكن من شيء؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Helpers offered to share their date palms; when the Prophet declined, they offered the harvest in exchange for the emigrants doing the work, and the emigrants agreed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r1.anchor: قالت الأنصار: اقسم بيننا وبين إخواننا النخيل، قال: لا فقالوا: تكفونا المؤنة ونشرككم في الثمرة، قالوا: سمعنا وأطعنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet offered the Helpers land in Bahrain; they would accept only if the emigrants received the same, and he told them they would face preferential treatment after him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r2.anchor: سمع أنس بن مالك حين خرج معه إلى الوليد قال: دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الأنصار إلى أن يقطع لهم البحرين، فقالوا: لا إلا أن تقطع لإخواننا من المهاجرين مثلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that at Banu Nadir the Prophet offered either sharing homes and property with the emigrants plus the booty, or keeping those possessions without a share of the booty; the Helpers chose to prefer the emigrants, and the verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم النضير للأنصار: "إن شئتم قسمتم للمهاجرين من أموالكم ودياركم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r4.claim: In Arabic “shuhh” means miserliness and withholding surplus; scholars distinguish it from ordinary stinginess.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r4.anchor: "والشح" في كلام العرب: البخل ومنع الفضل، وفرق العلماء بين الشح والبخل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r5.claim: Ibn Masud distinguishes the Qur’anic “shuhh,” consuming another’s wealth unjustly, from the man’s ordinary miserliness, which he calls blameworthy bukhl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r5.anchor: فقال عبد الله: ليس ذاك بالشح الذي ذكر الله عز وجل في القرآن، ولكن الشح أن تأكل مال أخيك ظلما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r6.claim: Ibn Umar says shuhh is not withholding one’s own wealth; it is coveting what belongs to someone else.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: ليس الشح أن يمنع الرجل ماله، إنما الشح أن تطمح عين الرجل إلى ما ليس له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr defines shuhh as taking unlawful wealth and withholding zakat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: "الشح" هو أخذ الحرام ومنع الزكاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r8.claim: Another definition is intense greed that drives a person to commit forbidden acts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p77/r8.anchor: وقيل: الشح هو الحرص الشديد الذي يحمله على ارتكاب المحارم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r7.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the emigrants and refers to the Helpers, whose commitment was manifest in settling in Medina and in faith.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r7.anchor: عطف على المهاجرين، والمراد بهم الأنصار

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r8.claim: One parsing supplies a deleted noun in the second phrase and a deleted genitive in the first, compensated by the lām; another takes it as settling the abode and sincerely embracing faith, illustrated by an unattributed poetic line.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r8.anchor: وقيل المعنى تبوءوا دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان فحذف المضاف من الثاني والمضاف إليه من الأول

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r9.claim: Another explanation says Medina was called faith because it is faith's manifestation and destination.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r9.anchor: وقيل سمى المدينة بالإيمان لأنها مظهره ومصيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r10.claim: The phrase means before the emigrants' migration; an alternate syntactic estimate attaches it to settling the abode while faith is a separate object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r10.anchor: من قبلهم } من قبل هجرة المهاجرين

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r11.claim: The Helpers love those who migrated to them and do not find them burdensome.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r11.anchor: يحبون من هاجر إليهم } ولا يثقل عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r12.claim: Here حاجة is whatever need gives rise to, such as a request, resentment, envy, or anger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r12.anchor: ما تحمل عليه الحاجة كالطلب والحزازة والحسد والغيظ

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r13.claim: What was given to the emigrants means their share of fayʾ and other gifts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r13.anchor: مما أعطي المهاجرون من الفيء وغيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r14.claim: They put the emigrants ahead of themselves, to the extent that a man with two wives would yield one and marry her to an emigrant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r14.anchor: ويقدمون المهاجرين على أنفسهم حتى إن كان عنده امرأتان نزل عن واحدة وزوجها من أحدهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r15.claim: Khaṣāṣa means need, from the gaps in a building.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r15.anchor: حاجة من خصاص البناء وهي فرجه

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r16.claim: One is protected from the soul's avarice by opposing its strong pull toward wealth and aversion to spending.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r16.anchor: حتى يخالفها فيما يغلب عليها من حب المال وبغض الإنفاق

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:8-9/r17.claim: The successful attain both immediate praise and reward in the hereafter.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p523/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p523/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p523/r1.claim: After explaining the distribution of fay and warning about the difficulty of accepting it, the text specifies its recipients, the central purpose of the allocation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p523/r1.anchor: وبين مصرف الفيء من القرى , وتهدد في المخالفة في ذلك لصعوبته على النفوس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r6.claim: After praising the emigrants and satisfying them with their allocation, the discourse praises the Ansar to console and thank them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r6.anchor: أتبعه مدحهم جبرا لهم وشكرا لصنيعهم فقال عاطفا على مجموع القصة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r7.claim: The Ansar made the city their settled home: it had been prepared for migration and victory, was their lasting place of residence, and was not a place to abandon for its blessing.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r7.anchor: أي جعلوا بغاية جهدهم { الدار } الكاملة في الدور

BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r8.claim: The author construes settling faith as keeping its company and holding fast to it as to a home one cannot do without.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r8.anchor: ولابسوه وصحبوه وخصوه بالصحبة ولزموه لزوما هو كلزوم المنزل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r9.claim: An alternate parsing treats faith as an attribute of the city: the conjunction marks firm possession of both qualities, and the city is called faith because faith is established and spreads from there.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p524/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الإيمان وصفا للدار بإعادة العاطف للإشارة إلى التمكن في كل من الوصفين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r1.claim: The Ansar stayed in the city out of love for faith, not for their property: faith's honor and public strength were fully realized there, otherwise they would have gone wherever the Prophet settled.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r1.anchor: لأجل أن أموالهم بها بل محبة في الإيمان علما منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r2.claim: من قبلهم means before the emigrants' migration, not the whole period since the Messenger's mission; the Ansar had already joined settled faith to settled residence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r2.anchor: أي قبل هجرة المهاجرين لأن وصفهم بالهجرة لم يكن إلا بعد إيجادها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r3.claim: Their settled faith before the emigrants arrived is a complete virtue: the emigrants only later combined faith and residence through migration.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r3.anchor: فالأنصار جمعوا التمكن في الإيمان إلى التمكن في الدار من قبل أن يجمع المهاجرون بينهما بالهجرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r4.claim: The Ansar continually renew their love for everyone who migrates to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r4.anchor: أخبر عنهم بقوله : { يحبون } أي على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r5.claim: An alternate parsing coordinates this clause with المهاجرين and makes it a circumstantial clause, thereby assigning the description jointly.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r5.anchor: وقيل العطف على المهاجرين , وهذه حال فيكون هذا حكما بالمشاركة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r6.claim: The destination phrase heightens the emigrants' claim on the Ansar: choosing them as their destination itself shows great love.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r6.anchor: لأن القصد إلى الإنسان يوجب حقه عليه لأنه لولا كمال محبته له ما خصه بالقصد إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r7.claim: The author cites the Ansar's sharing of their homes and wealth, and even offering to share their wives, as visible proof of their love; the emigrants declined the latter and accepted wealth.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r7.anchor: شاطروا المهاجرين في أموالهم وعرضوا عليهم أن يشاطروهم نساءهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r8.claim: They feel no need in their hearts, still less do they voice a request for what the emigrants received.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r8.anchor: التي هي مساكن قلوبهم فتصدر منها أوامر القلوب فضلا عن أن تنطق ألسنتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r9.claim: حاجة names the cause, need, in place of its result, asking for the emigrants' allocation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r9.anchor: وكان الحامل على طلب ذلك الحاجة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r10.claim: The allocation includes fay and any other gift, whoever gave it, even God and His Messenger; lacking a reason to ask makes envy or resentment still less likely.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r10.anchor: من الفيء وغيره من أموال بني النضير وغيرهم من أي مؤت كان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r11.claim: The verse strongly encourages brotherhood and warns against envy and resentment.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r11.anchor: فهذه الآية من أعظم حاث على حسن الإخاء محذر من الحسد والاستياء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r12.claim: يؤثرون means choosing the best things for others and giving them preferentially, whoever the recipient may be.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r12.anchor: يوقعون الأثرة وهي اختيار الأشياء الحسنة لغيرهم تخصيصا لهم بها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r13.claim: They prefer others over themselves; the author takes naming the self as evidence that they are thoroughly free of base traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r13.anchor: وذكر النفس دليل على أنهم في غاية النزاهة من الرذائل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r14.claim: خصاصة is poverty, a serious gap or need surrounding them, from the gaps in a building.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r14.anchor: أي فقر وخلل في الأحوال وحاجة شديدة تحيط بهم من كل جانب , من خصائص البناء وهي فرجه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r15.claim: The passive يُوقَ signals that overcoming the soul's vice is difficult and requires strong divine aid.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r15.anchor: وكان علاج الرذائل صعبا جدا , لا يطيقه الإنسان إلا بمعونة من الله شديدة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r16.claim: Protection from the soul's avarice means not withholding what one has and not coveting another's property out of envy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r16.anchor: فلا يكون مانعا لما عنده , حريصا على ما عند غيره حسدا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r17.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r17.claim: Ibn ʿUmar defines avarice as a man's eye aspiring to what is not his.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p525/r17.anchor: قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنه : الشح أن تطمح عين الرجل فيما ليس له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r1.claim: The Prophet warns that avarice destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to shed blood and violate what was forbidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r1.anchor: اتقوا الشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم , حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلو محارمهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r2.claim: Those purified from base traits are the truly elevated and fully successful, attaining every desired good.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r2.anchor: أي الكاملون في الفوز بكل مراد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r3.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri says a heart freed from attachments and possessions characterizes spiritual masters; one captive to worldly stakes remains preoccupied with transactions and demanding people's due, without tasting the spiritual path.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r3.anchor: قال القشيري : وتجرد القلب من الأعراض والأملاك صفة السادة والأكابر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r4.claim: When the emigrants arrived, the Ansar divided homes and property with them; after Banu Nadir's fay, the Prophet offered either a shared division while migrants stayed in Ansar homes, or the Banu Nadir property with the migrants leaving.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r4.anchor: وشرح الآية أن الأنصار كانوا لما قدم عليهم المهاجرون قسموا دورهم وأموالهم بينهم وبينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r5.claim: The Ansar chose to give the Banu Nadir allocation to the emigrants while they remained in the Ansar's homes; another version has them also offer a share of their own property.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r5.anchor: بل يقسم بين المهاجرين خاصة ويكونون في دورنا كما كانوا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r6.claim: The Prophet prayed for mercy upon the Ansar and their children.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r6.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( اللهم ارحم الأنصار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r7.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r7.claim: Abu Bakr praised the Ansar and thanked them for their generosity.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r7.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه : جزاكم الله خيرا يا معشر الأنصار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r8.speaker: العنزي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r8.claim: Al-ʿAnazi's poem compares the Ansar's support to rescuing companions when their footing slipped, and says they would have tired of the burden only if they had suffered the same hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p526/r8.anchor: كما قال العنزي : جزى الله عنا جعفرا حين أزلقت بنا نعلنا

DURR-FULL:v8p101/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p101/r4.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p101/r4.claim: Umar reads the fay verses as allocating the fund among the Prophet's listed groups—Muhājirūn, Anṣār, and later Muslims—rather than exclusively to any one group.
DURR-FULL:v8p101/r4.anchor: ثم والله ما جعلها لهؤلاء وحدهم حتى قال: {والذين تبوؤوا الدار والإيمان} إلى {المفلحون}

DURR-FULL:v8p102/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r1.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r1.claim: Umar contrasts the poor-recipient categories of charity with the fay allocations to Muhājirūn, Anṣār, and later Muslims, then says the public fund is for Muslims generally, including a shepherd.
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r1.anchor: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب {إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين} حتى بلغ {عليم حكيم} ثم قال: هذه لهؤلاء ثم قرأ {ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى}

DURR-FULL:v8p102/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r2.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r2.claim: Umar says Qur'anic allocations show that every Muslim has a right in the public funds, whether paid or withheld, down to a shepherd in Aden.
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: اجتمعوا لهذا المال فأنظروا لمن ترونه

DURR-FULL:v8p102/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r3.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r3.claim: Umar states that every Muslim on earth has a right to this public money, except what is privately owned.
DURR-FULL:v8p102/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: ما على وجه الأرض مسلم إلا وله في هذا المال حق إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم

DURR-FULL:v8p106/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r1.claim: A report lists ten names for Medina: al-Madīna, Ṭayba, Ṭāba, Miskīna, Jābira, Majbūra, Tabaddud, Yathrib, and al-Dār.
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: للمدينة عشرة أسماء هي المدينة وهي طيبة وطابة ومسكينة

DURR-FULL:v8p106/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r2.claim: When a hungry visitor arrived, an Anṣārī host and his wife put their children to bed, darkened the lamp, and let the guest eat their only food; the Prophet said God admired them and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: أتى رجل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله أصابني الجهد فأرسل إلى نسائه فلم يجد عندهن شيئا

DURR-FULL:v8p106/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r3.speaker: ثابت بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r3.claim: Thābit ibn Qays hosted a fasting Muslim and, with his family, pretended to eat in darkness while the guest ate their single loaf; the Prophet said God admired them and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p106/r3.anchor: عن أبي المتوكل الناجي رضي الله عنه أن رجلا من المسلمين مكث صائما ثلاثة أيام يمسي فلا يجد ما يفطر فيصبح صائما حتى فطن له رجل من الأنصار يقال له ثابت بن قيس

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r1.claim: A report authenticated by al-Ḥākim says a Companion passed a sheep's head to a needier household; it circulated among seven homes and returned to him, occasioning the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r1.anchor: أهدي لرجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأس شاة فقال: إن أخي فلانا وعياله أحوج إلى هذا منا

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r2.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r2.claim: Muqātil glosses خصاصة as poverty or need.

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd distinguishes ordinary miserliness from Qur'anic شح: the latter is consuming another person's property unjustly.
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن رجلا قال له: إني أخاف أن أكون قد هلكت قال: وما ذاك قال: إني سمعت الله يقول: {ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون}

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says شح is not merely withholding one's own wealth; it is coveting what belongs to others.
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r4.anchor: قال: ليس الشحيح أن يمنع الرجل ماله ولكنه البخل وإنه لشر

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan counts looking at a woman one does not own as an instance of شح.
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: النظر إلى المرأة لا يملكها من الشح

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r6.speaker: طاووس
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r6.claim: Ṭāwūs distinguishes bukhl, withholding what one has, from شح, coveting what other people have.
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r6.anchor: عن طاووس رضي الله عنه قال: البخلان يبخل الإنسان بما في يديه والشح أن يشح على ما في أيدي الناس

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf repeatedly prayed for protection from his soul's شح, explaining that this would keep him from stealing, adultery, and other wrongdoing.
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r7.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أنه كان يطوف بالبيت يقول: اللهم قني شح نفسي لا يزيد على ذلك فقيل له فقال: إذا وقيت شح نفسي لا أسرق

DURR-FULL:v8p107/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p107/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains شح as taking unlawful property and withholding zakat.

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r1.claim: ʿAlī says paying one's zakat protects one from the soul's شح.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: من أدى زكاة ماله فقد وقي شح نفسه

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r2.speaker: ابن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says شح is worse than bukhl: it clings to one's own wealth and seeks to take others' wealth, while bukhl concerns only one's own.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمرو قال: الشح أشد من البخل لأن الشحيح يشح على ما في يديه فيحبسه ويشح على ما في أيدي الناس

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r3.claim: A report says God created the Garden of Eden, which answered with a verse from Sūrat al-Muʾminūn; God swore that no miser would dwell there, and the Prophet recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r3.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: خلق الله جنة عدن ثم قال لها: انطقي فقالت: (قد أفلح المؤمنون)

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r4.claim: The Prophet says three acts free a person from شح: paying zakat, hosting a guest, and giving during hardship.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: ثلاث من كن فيه فقد برئ من الشح من أدى زكاة ماله

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r5.claim: The Prophet says nothing has harmed Islam as much as شح.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r5.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما محق الإسلام محق الشح شيء قط

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r6.speaker: أبو زرعة
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r6.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says a heart's poverty is not remedied by abundant worldly wealth and that its شح harms the person himself.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r6.anchor: عن أبي زرعة قالك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من كان الفقر في قلبه فلا يغنيه ما أكثر له في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r7.speaker: خالد بن يزيد بن جارية
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r7.claim: A second report says one is free of شح by paying zakat, hosting a guest, and giving in times of need.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r7.anchor: عن مجمع بن يحيى بن جارية قال: حدثني عمي خالد بن يزيد بن جارية رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: برئ من الشح من أدى الزكاة

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r8.claim: The Prophet says faith and شح never coexist in a servant's heart; he also says dust from God's path and Hell's smoke do not meet in a servant's body.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا يجتمع غبار في سبيل الله ودخان جهنم في جوف عبد أبدا ولا يجتمع الشح والإيمان

DURR-FULL:v8p108/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r9.claim: The Prophet says miserliness and ill suspicion never coexist in a Muslim's heart.
DURR-FULL:v8p108/r9.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: خصلتان لا يجتمعان في جوف مسلم البخل وسوء الظن

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says khasasah here means need or poverty.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل رضي الله عنه في قوله : ولو كان بهم خصاصة قال : فاقة .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r2.claim: In al-Aswad ibn Hilal's report, Abd Allah defines Qur'anic shuhh as wrongfully consuming one's brother's wealth, distinguishing it from ordinary miserliness, which he condemns.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3346#2/r2.anchor: فقال له عبد الله : ليس ذلك بالشح الذي ذكر الله في القران ، انما الشح الذي ذكر الله في القران ان تاكل مال اخيك ظلما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r2.claim: The most likely parsing coordinates “those who settled the abode” with “the emigrants” in the preceding verse; these settlers are the Anṣār.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r2.anchor: الأظهر أن { الذين } عطف على { المهاجرين } ( الحشر : 8 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r3.claim: “Those who settled the abode” refers to the Anṣār.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r4.claim: Dār can mean a land or a tribe’s original territory, and can also denote a town; al-Aʿrāf 7:78 uses it for the Thamūd settlement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r4.anchor: والدار تطلق على البلاد ، وأصلها موضع القبيلة من الأرض . وأطلقت على القرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r5.claim: The definite article identifies the abode as Yathrib, and the wording presents the Anṣār as its people before describing their love for emigrants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r5.anchor: والتعريف هنا للعهد لأن المراد بالدار : يثرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r6.claim: Tabawwuʾ means taking a place as one’s dwelling, a place to which one returns after going about one’s affairs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r6.anchor: والتبوء : اتخاذ المباءة وهي البقعة التي يبوء إليها صاحبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r7.claim: One exegetical reading makes the construction a metaphoric allusion that treats faith as a dwelling and “settling” as both literal and figurative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r7.anchor: أحدهما أن يجعل الكلام استعارة مكنية بتشبيه الإيمان بالمنزل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r8.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r8.claim: Most exegetes supply a verb such as “and they sincerely embraced faith,” understood from context, rather than making “faith” a direct object of “settled.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r8.anchor: وجمهور المفسرين جعلوا المعطوف عاملا مقدرا يدل عليه الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r9.speaker: الراجز الذي لا يعرف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r9.claim: The unidentified rajaz line supports supplying an omitted verb with the coordinated noun: she was fed dates and [given] cold water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r9.anchor: نحو قول الراجز الذي لا يعرف : علفتها تبنا وماء باردا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبعرى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r10.claim: Ibn al-Zibʿarā’s verse supports an omitted verb with the coordinated noun, “and [holding] a spear.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r10.anchor: وقول عبد الله بن الزبعرى : يا ليت زوجكك قد غدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers parsing the waw as comitative and “faith” as an object of accompaniment, though few commentators accept this analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r11.anchor: وعندي أن هذا أحسن الوجوه ، وإن قل قائلوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r12.speaker: جمهور البصريين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r12.claim: Most grammarians treat the comitative object as attested but rare and require the verb governing it to govern its companion noun as well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r12.anchor: والجمهور يجعلون النصب على المفعول معه سماعيا فهو عندهم قليل الاستعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r13.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r13.claim: Ibn Hishām claimed in Mughnī al-Labīb that the comitative object does not occur in the Qurʾān with certainty, interpreting 10:71 accordingly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r13.anchor: حتى ادعى ابن هشام في ( مغني اللبيب ) أنه غير واقع في القرآن بيقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r14.speaker: البصريون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r14.claim: The Basrans require the verb governing an object of accompaniment to govern the noun accompanying it; the Kufans and al-Akhfash instead allow the waw to mean “with.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r14.anchor: لأن جمهور البصريين يشترطون أن يكون العامل في المفعول معه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r15.speaker: الأخفش
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash and the Kufans allow the comitative waw itself to govern, since it means “with”; ʿAbd al-Qāhir likewise says the waw governs the noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p89/r15.anchor: خلافا للكوفيين والأخفش فإن الواو عندهم بمعنى ( مع )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r1.claim: A comitative noun need not be governed by the same verb as its companion, as shown by ordinary expressions about water and a ruler traveling with the Nile.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r1.anchor: والحق عدم التزام أن يكون المفعول معه معمولا للفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r2.claim: The Anṣār are praised because they made the migration city their home and sheltered emigrants as a community of believers unlike any other at the time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r2.anchor: وهو يفيد الثناء عليهم بأن دار الهجرة دارهم آووا إليها المهاجرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r3.claim: “Before them” modifies only “settled”; the comitative waw is not coordination and functions like an adverb, so it cannot carry the preceding preposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r3.anchor: وبذلك يتضح أن متعلق { من قبلهم } فعل { تبوؤا } بمفرده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r4.claim: Mentioning the city alongside faith hints at Medina’s distinction, treating their settlement there as a companion to their faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r4.anchor: وفي ذكر الدار ( وهي المدينة ) مع ذكر الإيمان إيماء إلى فضيلة المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r5.claim: Ibn Wahb reports hearing Mālik say that Medina was established through faith and migration, unlike other towns conquered by the sword; Mālik cited this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r5.anchor: فيما رواه عنه ابن وهب قال : سمعت مالكا يذكر فضل المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r6.speaker: author
