IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r6.claim: The clause describing love for those who emigrated is circumstantial and praises the Anṣār’s established Islamic brotherhood, unusual among tribes receiving newcomers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r6.anchor: وجملة { يحبون من هاجر إليهم } حال من الذين تبوؤوا الدار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r7.speaker: سعد بن الربيع
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r7.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ recounts Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ offering ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf half his wealth and one of his wives; the Anṣār housed emigrants and shared their palms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r7.anchor: ما ثبت في ( الصحيح ) من خبر سعد بن الربيع مع عبد الرحمن بن عوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r8.claim: The Prophet’s pairing of emigrants and Anṣār as brothers is a sufficient illustration of the love praised here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p91/r8.anchor: وحسبك الأخوة التي آخى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين المهاجرين والأنصار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r1.claim: “Finding” means mental perception; denying that they find a desire figuratively denies that it exists, since they would otherwise perceive it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r1.anchor: وكنى بانتفاء وجدان الحاجة عن انتفاء وجودها لأنها لو كانت موجودة لأدركوها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r2.claim: The poet’s line about not seeing a lizard burrow illustrates the figurative use of perception to imply the existence of something.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r2.anchor: من باب قول الشاعر : ولا ترى الضب بها ينجحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r3.claim: Ḥājah first means the need itself, then the needed object; here it figuratively means a desired aim, a common usage comparable to literal meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r3.anchor: والحاجة في الأصل : اسم مصدر الحوج وهو الاحتياج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r4.claim: The same usage means an aim in al-Muʾmin 40:80 and the purpose Jacob fulfilled in Yūsuf 12:68; al-Nābighah uses it for concealed aims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r4.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r5.claim: The preposition “from” marks the desire as originating in the spoils granted to the emigrants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r5.anchor: وعليه فتكون ( من ) في قوله : { مما أوتوا } ابتدائية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r6.claim: “Their breasts” means their selves or inner life, as when “heart” denotes the inward faculties.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r6.anchor: والصدور مراد بها النفوس جمع الصدر وهو الباطن الذي فيه الحواس الباطنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r7.claim: What the emigrants received was the Fayʾ of Banū al-Naḍīr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r7.anchor: و ( ما أوتوا ) هو فيء بني النضير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r8.claim: The pronoun in “their breasts” refers to the Anṣār, while the pronoun in “they were given” refers to the emigrants; the latter follows the plural sense of “who.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r8.anchor: وضمير { صدورهم } عائد إلى { الذين تبوؤا الدار } ، وضمير { أوتوا } عائد إلى { من هاجر إليهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r9.claim: Nearby third-person pronouns can resolve to different antecedents by context; the example from al-Rūm 30:9 and Ibn Mirdās’s poem illustrate this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r9.anchor: مثل ( ما ) في قوله تعالى : { وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها في سورة الروم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r10.claim: The Anṣār did not secretly aspire to take any portion of the Banū al-Naḍīr spoils given to the emigrants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p92/r10.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم لا يخامر نفوسهم تشوف إلى أخذ شيء مما أوتيه المهاجرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r1.claim: Alternatively, ḥājah retains its literal sense of need, which can exist in the breast as an emotion; love made the Anṣār feel no lack of anything given to emigrants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r1.anchor: ويجوز وجه آخر بأن يحمل لفظ حاجة على استعماله الحقيقي اسم مصدر الاحتياج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r2.claim: “From what they were given” can be causal or source-marking; either reading denies felt need and its ordinary roots in rivalry and envy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r2.anchor: وتكون ( من ) في قوله تعالى : مما أوتوا } للتعليل ، أي حاجة لأجل ما أوتيه المهاجرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r3.claim: The omitted complement is “a need for anything the emigrants were given”; denying its causes also rules out its usual antecedents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r3.anchor: وقد دل انتفاء أسباب الحاجة على متعلق حاجة المحذوف إذ التقدير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r4.claim: Īthār means preferring one thing over another as an act of virtue or benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r4.anchor: والإيثار : ترجيح شيء على غيره بمكرمة أو منفعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r5.claim: The Anṣār deliberately preferred the emigrants, an even higher degree than lacking desire; the object is omitted because the earlier mention of what they received supplies it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r5.anchor: وهذا أعلى درجة مما أفاده قوله : { ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r6.speaker: الأنصار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r6.claim: In a report in Ṣaḥīḥ, the Prophet offered the Anṣār plots of Bahrain’s palm groves; they refused unless their emigrant brothers received equal plots.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r6.anchor: ما روي في ( الصحيح ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا الأنصار ليقطع لهم قطائع بنخل البحرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r7.claim: Al-Bukhārī’s report from Abū Hurayrah tells how Abū Ṭalḥah hosted a hungry visitor, putting the children to bed and extinguishing the lamp so the guest could eat their only food.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p93/r7.anchor: فما رواه البخاري عن أبي هريرة قال : ( أتى رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r1.claim: The concessive “even if” means they would prefer others despite severe need, so they surely did so under easier conditions; it does not imply impossibility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r1.anchor: والتقدير : لو كان بهم خصاصة لآثروا على أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr compares the concessive construction with al-ʿImrān 3:91, where payment is rejected even if one offers the earth’s full weight in gold as ransom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r2.anchor: وقد بينا ذلك عند قوله تعالى : { فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r4.claim: The feminine verb is used because khaṣāṣah is not truly feminine and because a prepositional phrase separates the verb from its subject; the bāʾ denotes circumstantial association.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r4.anchor: وتذكير فعل كان } لأجل كون تأنيث الخصاصة ليس حقيقيا ، ولأنه فصل بين { كان } واسمها بالمجرور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r5.claim: The closing sentence is an epilogue and parenthetical summation: protection from greed explains how they could prefer others even while needy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r5.anchor: وجملة { ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون } تذييل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r6.claim: Their generosity even in hardship signals freedom from avarice; whoever is spared some of its blameworthy forms succeeds to that extent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r6.anchor: يشير إلى أن إيثارهم على أنفسهم حتى في حالة الخصاصة هو سلامة من شح الأنفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r7.claim: Shuḥḥ, with either vowel on the first consonant, is an innate impulse to withhold what belongs to oneself and is close to miserliness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r7.anchor: والشح بضم الشين وكسرها : غريزة في النفس بمنع ما هو لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r8.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r8.claim: Al-Ṭībī says the distinction between greed and miserliness is difficult; al-Kashshāf’s account makes miserliness an effect of greed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r8.anchor: وقال الطيبي : الفرق بين الشح والبخل عسير جدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r9.claim: The phrase “souls are made present with greed” in al-Nisāʾ 4:128 depicts greed as an innate trait that stays with a person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r9.anchor: وقد قال تعالى : { وأحضرت الأنفس الشح } ( النساء : 128 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r10.claim: A hadith identifies the best charity as giving while healthy and miserly, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث في بيان أفضل الصدقة ( أن تصدق وأنت صحيح شحيح تخشى الفقر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r11.claim: Greed varies in degree; it is blameworthy when it leads someone to withhold good, and the blame depends on what is withheld.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p94/r11.anchor: فإذا غلب عليها بمنع المعروف والخير فذلك مذموم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r1.speaker: الشاعر الذي لم يقف على قائله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r1.claim: An unattributed poet depicts a constricted soul resisting good deeds, illustrating the force of greed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r1.anchor: يمارس نفسا بين جنبيه كزة إذا هم بالمعروف قالت له مهلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r2.claim: Being protected from greed means not acquiring it as a blameworthy character; protection from all of it avoids blame, while partial protection brings proportional success.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r2.anchor: فمن وقي شح نفسه ، أي وقي من أن يكون الشح المذموم خلقا له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r3.claim: The demonstrative honors this group, and the emphatic restriction magnifies their success as though all success belonged to those protected from greed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r3.anchor: واسم الإشارة لتعظيم هذا الصنف من الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r4.speaker: من المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r4.claim: Some exegetes treat the Anṣār as a new sentence of praise and deny them any share in the Fayʾ, restricting the preceding allocation to named towns and reporting that they ceded the spoils to emigrants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r4.anchor: ومن المفسرين من جعل { والذين تبوؤا الدار } ابتداء كلام للثناء على الأنصار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r5.speaker: منهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r5.claim: Another group restricts this verse to the Fayʾ of Banū al-Naḍīr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r5.anchor: ومنهم من قصر هذه الآية على فيء بني النضير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects both readings as disrupting the sūrah’s coherence and relying on weak reports; he instead joins the Anṣār to the preceding group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r6.anchor: وكل ذلك خروج عن مهيع انتظام آي هذه السورة بعضها مع بعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r7.speaker: من المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r7.claim: On the independent-sentence reading, “they love those who emigrated to them” is the predicate of the relative subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p95/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير يكون عطف { والذين تبوؤا الدار } عطف جملة على جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r1.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r1.claim: A parsing attributed by Ibn al-Faras to al-Shafiʿi coordinates 59:9 with 59:8 and treats 59:10 as a new sentence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r1.anchor: ونسبه ابن الفرس في ( أحكام القرآن ) إلى الشافعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r2.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is reported to hold that when fayʾ is land, the imam may choose its disposition; it need not go to the listed recipients of Banu Nadir’s fayʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p97/r2.anchor: ونسبه ابن الفرس في ( أحكام القرآن ) إلى الشافعي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.claim: Those who settled are the Ansar, and al-dār is Medina; the pronoun in before them refers to the Muhajirun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.anchor: الذين تبوؤا هم الأنصار، والضمير في قبلهم للمهاجرين، و «الدار» هي المدينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.claim: They settled in Medina together with faith; pairing faith with a place is eloquent, since faith is not literally a place, and the phrasing admits several elegant analyses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى: تبوءوا الدار مع الإيمان معا، وبهذا الاقتران يصح معنى قوله: من قبلهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.claim: God praises the Ansar for loving the Muhajirun and preferring them over themselves, and says they have been protected from greed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.anchor: وأثنى الله تعالى في هذه الآية على الأنصار بأنهم يحبون المهاجرين، وبأنهم يؤثرون على أنفسهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains ḥājah here as envy; the verse praises the Ansar for not begrudging what the Muhajirun received.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.anchor: والحاجة: الحسد في هذا الموضع، قاله الحسن وتعم بعد جميع الوجوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.claim: The passive verb means they were given something; its unexpressed subject is the Muhajirun, including the property and villages of Banū al-Naḍīr distributed by the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.anchor: وأوتوا معناه: أعطوا، والضمير المرفوع بأن لم يسم فاعله هو للمهاجرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.claim: The clause about preferring others describes the Ansar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ويؤثرون الآية، صفة للأنصار.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r7.speaker: أبو المتوكل وأبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r7.claim: A report says the verse arose from one Ansari hosting a guest: Abu al-Mutawakkil names him Thābit ibn Qays, while Abu Hurayra in Makki's book gives the kunya Abū Ṭalḥa; the couple served the guest and feigned eating.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو المتوكل: هو ثابت بن قيس، وقال أبي هريرة في كتاب مكي: كنية هذا الرجل أبو طلحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r8.claim: In the hosting report, the Prophet said God admired the couple's conduct the previous night, and the verse was revealed about it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r8.anchor: قال: عجب الله من فعلكما البارحة، ونزلت الآية في ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r9.claim: Preferring someone else at personal cost is the noblest character trait.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r10.speaker: حذيفة العدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r10.claim: At Yarmuk, Ḥudhayfa al-ʿAdawī sought his wounded cousin with water; the cousin sent him to another, who sent him onward, and all three died before he could give them a drink.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p287#2/r10.anchor: وقال حذيفة العدوي: طلبت يوم اليرموك ابن عم لي في الجرحى ومعي شيء من ماء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r1.speaker: أبو زيد البسطامي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r1.claim: Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī recounts a young pilgrim from Balkh challenging his definition of asceticism: real zuhd is enduring when food is absent and preferring others when it is available.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r1.anchor: قدم علينا شاب من بلخ حاجا فقال: ما حد الزهد عندكم؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r2.claim: Another occasion report says the Prophet offered the Ansar a choice: divide their homes and wealth with the Muhajirun and share the booty, or keep their property and leave the booty to the Muhajirun; they chose to share their own and leave it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r2.anchor: وروي: أن سبب هذه الآية أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قسم هذه القرى في المهاجرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r3.claim: Khaṣāṣah means poverty and need; its root evokes gaps and openings between the timbers of a house, like the deficiencies in a poor person's condition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r3.anchor: والخصاصة: الفاقة والحاجة، وهو مأخوذ من خصائص البيت وهو ما يبقى بين عيدانه من الفرج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r4.claim: Shuḥḥ is intense withholding of wealth, attachment to it, desire for it, and long hopes; it is a source of every bad trait.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r4.anchor: شح النفس» هو كثرة منعها وضبطها على المال والرغبة فيه وامتداد الأمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r5.claim: The Prophet says paying obligatory zakat, hosting a guest, and giving in a calamity clear a person of shuḥḥ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r5.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من أدى الزكاة المفروضة وقرى الضيف وأعطى في النائبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls shuḥḥ an inner poverty that wealth cannot cure, but instead increases and exhausts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: «شح النفس» فقر لا يذهبه غنى المال بل يزيده وينصب به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r7.claim: Abd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf used to pray while circumambulating only that God protect him from the greed of his own soul; if protected, he said, he would do no wrong.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r7.anchor: كان عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله عنه يطوف ويقول: اللهم قني شح نفسي، لا يزيد على ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r8.speaker: ابن زيد وابن جبير وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd, Ibn Jubayr, and others say a person avoids shuḥḥ by taking nothing God forbids and not withholding obligatory zakat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وابن جبير وجماعة: من لم يأخذ شيئا نهاه الله تعالى عنه ولم يمنع الزكاة المفروضة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd defines shuḥḥ as consuming another's property unlawfully; refusing to give one's own is bukhl, blameworthy but distinct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r9.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود رحمه الله «شح النفس» : هو أكل مال الغير بالباطل، وأما منع الإنسان ماله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r10.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar read shīḥ, with kasra on the initial consonant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r10.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عمر: «شح» بكسر السين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r11.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r11.claim: Abū Ḥaywah read yuqawwa, with fatḥa on the wāw and a doubled qāf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: «يوق» بفتح الواو وشد القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r12.claim: The form yūqā follows the pattern yafʿal from waqā–yaqī, like wazana–yazinu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r12.anchor: يفعل من وقى يقي مثل وزن يزن.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p288/r13.claim: Al-mufliḥūn are those who attain what they seek.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r1.claim: Al-dar is the abode of emigration, Medina; the phrase about faith is fronted and delayed, referring to the Ansar’s faith before the emigrants arrived.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r1.anchor: يعني دار الهجرة وهي المدينة والإيمان من قبلهم فيها تقديم وتأخير تقديره والذين تبوؤوا الدار من قبلهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r2.claim: On the rearranged reading, faith is formally coordinated with abode but not semantically, since faith is not a place one can inhabit; the sense is that they preferred faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r2.anchor: والإيمان عطف على الدار في الظاهر لا في المعنى لأن الإيمان ليس بمكان يتبوأ وإنما تقديره وآثروا الإيمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r3.claim: The emigrants accepted Islam before the Ansar, while the Ansar inhabited Medina before the emigrants; an alternative retains the wording’s surface sense of settling in abode and faith before migration.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r3.anchor: وإسلام المهاجرين قبل الأنصار وسكنى الأنصار المدينة قبل المهاجرين وقيل الكلام على ظاهره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r4.claim: The Ansar loved the emigrants and shared their homes and property with them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r4.anchor: يحبون من هاجر إليهم وذلك أنهم شاركوهم في منازلهم وأموالهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r5.claim: The need or grievance in their hearts means envy and anger over what the emigrants received.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r5.anchor: أي حسدا وغيظا مما أوتي المهاجرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r6.claim: Hasan says what the emigrants received was the fay; the Prophet distributed Banu al-Nadir’s property among them, giving it to only three Ansar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r6.anchor: أحدهما مال الفيء قاله الحسن وقد ذكرنا آنفا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم أموال بني النضير بين المهاجرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r7.claim: The other interpretation is that what the emigrants received was distinction and precedence.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r8.claim: The Ansar preferred the emigrants in wealth and homes despite their own poverty and need, so their generosity did not come from abundance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r8.anchor: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم بأموالهم ومنازلهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة أي فقر وحاجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r9.claim: A report in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim tells of an Ansari host who fed a starving guest by pretending to eat while his family went hungry; the Prophet said God marveled at their deed. Some versions identify the guest as one of the People of the Bench.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p212/r9.anchor: أخرجه البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين من حديث أبي هريرة وفي بعض الألفاظ عن أبي هريرة أن الضيف كان من أهل الصفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that a sheep’s head was passed among seven households, each preferring another family, before returning to the first; the verse was revealed about this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r1.anchor: أن رجلا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أهدي له رأس شاة فقال إن أخي فلانا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r2.claim: Anas reports a similar account: a roasted sheep’s head passed through nine needy people and returned to its first recipient, occasioning the verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r2.anchor: وروي نحو هذه القصة عن أنس بن مالك قال أهدي لبعض الصحابة رأس شاة مشوي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r3.speaker: ابن السميفع وأبو رجاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa and Abu Rajaʾ read yuwaqqa with a doubled qaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع وأبو رجاء ومن يوق بتشديد القاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r4.claim: The commentators explain protection from miserliness as neither taking what God forbids nor withholding what He commands one to give; the Ansar showed it by freely leaving the fay to the emigrants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون هو أن لا يأخذ شيئا مما نهاه الله عنه ولا يمنع شيئا أمره الله بأدائه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir defines shuh in Arabic as withholding surplus wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r5.anchor: فقال ابن جرير الشح في كلام العرب هو منع الفضل من المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r6.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r6.claim: Al-Khattabi says shuh is more intense than bukhl: shuh is a broad, inborn disposition, while bukhl usually concerns particular things.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r6.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الخطابي الشح أبلغ في المنع من البخل وإنما الشح بمنزلة الجنس والبخل بمنزلة النوع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r7.claim: An authority quoted by al-Khattabi distinguishes bukhl as stinginess with one’s money and shuh as stinginess with both money and generosity or good offices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r7.anchor: وحكى الخطابي عن بعضهم أنه قال البخل أن يضن بماله والشح أن يبخل بماله ومعروفه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r8.claim: Ibn Masud tells a man who feared damnation because he rarely gave that Quranic shuh is consuming another’s wealth unjustly; mere stinginess is bukhl and a bad trait.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r8.anchor: روى أبو الشعثاء أن رجلا أتى ابن مسعود فقال إني أخاف أن أكون قد هلكت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r9.speaker: رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r9.claim: The Prophet says one is free of shuh by paying zakat, honoring a guest, and giving in adversity; Anas ibn Malik transmits the report.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p214/r9.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال برئ من الشح من أدى الزكاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r2.claim: The Anṣar settled in the abode of migration before the migrants and believed before many of them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r2.anchor: أي: سكنوا دار الهجرة من قبل المهاجرين وآمنوا قبل كثير منهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r3.claim: Umar urged the next caliph to recognize the first migrants' rights and honor, and to treat the Anṣar well, accepting their good deeds and forgiving their wrongdoers; al-Bukhari transmits it here too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p68#2/r3.anchor: قال عمر: وأوصي الخليفة [من] (1) بعدي بالمهاجرين الأولين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r1.claim: The Anṣar's generosity and noble character led them to love the migrants and support them from their wealth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r1.anchor: أي: من كرمهم وشرف أنفسهم، يحبون المهاجرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r2.claim: Anas reports that migrants praised the Anṣar for supporting them in scarcity and giving generously, sharing pleasant livelihood and expenses; they feared the Anṣar would take all the reward. The Prophet replied that they would not, as long as migrants praised them and prayed for them. Ibn Kathir had not seen this route in the books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r2.anchor: قال المهاجرون: يا رسول الله، ما رأينا مثل قوم قدمنا عليهم أحسن مواساة في قليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r3.claim: Anas reports that when the Prophet offered the Anṣar lands in Bahrain, they would accept only if migrants received the same; the Prophet told them to be patient until they met him because favoritism would follow his death. Bukhari alone transmits this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r3.anchor: دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الأنصار أن يقطع لهم البحرين، قالوا: لا إلا أن تقطع لإخواننا من المهاجرين مثلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Anṣar offered to share their date palms with the migrants; the Prophet declined, so they offered to tend them and share the harvest, and the migrants accepted. Bukhari transmits this without Muslim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69/r4.anchor: قالت الأنصار: اقسم بيننا وبين إخواننا النخيل. قال: لا. فقالوا: تكفونا المؤنة ونشرككم في الثمرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.claim: The Ansar bear no envy over the migrants' favored rank, honor, and precedence in mention.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.anchor: ولا يجدون في أنفسهم حسدا للمهاجرين فيما فضلهم الله به من المنزلة والشرف، والتقديم في الذكر والرتبة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the absence of need in their hearts as absence of envy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.anchor: قال: الحسن البصري: {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة} يعني: الحسد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.claim: Qatada takes what was given to mean what the migrants' brothers received.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني فيما أعطى إخوانهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise understands the phrase as what was given to their brothers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet named an Anṣārī for Paradise three days; ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr found little night worship, but the man bore no ill will or envy toward Muslims, which Abdullah said won his rank.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.anchor: عن أنس قال: كنا جلوسا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: "يطلع عليكم الآن رجل من أهل الجنة".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r1.claim: Al-Nasa'i transmits the Anas report with Ma'mar's chain, which Ibn Kathir calls sound by the standards of the two Ṣaḥīḥs; ʿAqīl and others instead add an unnamed man between al-Zuhrī and Anas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح على شرط الصحيحين، لكن رواه عقيل وغيره عن الزهري، عن رجل، عن أنس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd explicitly says the gift in question was what had been given to the emigrants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في قوله: {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا} يعني {مما أوتوا} المهاجرون.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir links the phrase to some Ansar discussing the Banu al-Naḍīr property, for which God reproached them by citing the rule that the spoils were granted to the Messenger without a cavalry charge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r3.anchor: وتكلم في أموال بني النضير بعض من تكلم من الأنصار، فعاتبهم الله في ذلك، فقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r4.claim: In Ibn Zayd's account, the Prophet told the Ansar that the emigrants had left wealth and children; they first offered shared property, then accepted an arrangement to support them and divide the fruit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70/r4.anchor: وقال رسول الله: "إن إخوانكم قد تركوا الأموال والأولاد وخرجوا إليكم". فقالوا: أموالنا بيننا قطائع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r1.claim: They put the needy before themselves, giving to others first even while they themselves need what they give.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r1.anchor: يعني: حاجة، أي: يقدمون المحاويج على حاجة أنفسهم، ويبدءون بالناس قبلهم في حال احتياجهم إلى ذلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says the best charity is the effort made by someone with little.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r2.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " أفضل الصدقة جهد المقل".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r3.claim: Their self-sacrifice exceeds giving while loving one's wealth, as in 76:8 and 2:177, because they give despite their own need.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r3.anchor: وهؤلاء آثروا على أنفسهم مع خصاصتهم وحاجتهم إلى ما أنفقوه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakr gave all his wealth; when asked what remained for his family, he answered that he had left them God and His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r4.anchor: فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما أبقيت لأهلك؟ ". فقال: أبقيت لهم الله ورسوله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة وأصحابه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r5.claim: At Yarmuk, wounded companions successively directed water to one another; by the time it reached the third, they had all died without drinking.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r5.anchor: وهذا (2) الماء الذي عرض (3) على عكرمة وأصحابه يوم اليرموك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports an Ansari couple who hosted the Prophet's starving guest, put their children to sleep, extinguished the lamp, and ate nothing; the Prophet said God marveled or laughed at them, and the verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p70#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أتى رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، أصابني الجهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r1.claim: Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i transmit the guest-hosting report in similar form; Muslim identifies the Ansari as Abu Talha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r1.anchor: وفي رواية لمسلم تسمية هذا الأنصاري بأبي طلحة، رضي الله عنه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r2.claim: Whoever is protected from the soul's avarice has succeeded and prospered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r2.anchor: أي: من سلم من الشح فقد أفلح وأنجح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r3.claim: The Prophet warns against oppression and avarice: avarice destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and violation of sacred limits; Muslim alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r3.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إياكم والظلم، فإن الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة، واتقوا الشح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r4.claim: The Prophet warns against oppression, obscenity, and avarice, which led earlier peoples to injustice, immorality, and severing kinship; Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اتقوا الظلم؛ فإن الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة، واتقوا الفحش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r5.claim: The Prophet says that faith and avarice cannot coexist in a servant's heart, just as the dust of God's path and Hell's smoke cannot coexist in it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "لا يجتمع غبار في سبيل الله ودخان جهنم في جوف عبد أبدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r6.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r6.claim: Asked about the verse, Abdullah distinguishes its shuhh from ordinary miserliness: Quranic shuhh is consuming one's brother's property unjustly; miserliness is still a bad trait.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p71/r6.anchor: عبد الله: ليس ذلك (5) بالشح الذي ذكر الله في القرآن، إنما الشح الذي ذكر الله في القرآن أن تأكل مال أخيك ظلما

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r1.claim: بوأته منزلا means that I settled or lodged him in a dwelling; المباءة is the dwelling place.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r1.anchor: بوأته منزلا: إذا أسكنته إياه، وقيل: المباءة المنزل

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r2.claim: خصاصة means poverty or need, and can mean a gap or opening; it is related to being left alone without what one needs.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r2.anchor: والخصاصة: الإملاق، وكل ثلمة خصاصة، وأصله الاختصاص، وهو الانفراد بالأمر

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r3.claim: Another explanation treats خصاصة and خلّة as synonyms for need; its root image is a gap, as when the moon appears through a break in cloud or a hut has openings.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r3.anchor: وقيل: الخصاصة والخلة سواء، وأصله الفرجة، يقال للقمر: بدا من خصاصة الغيم

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r4.claim: Shuḥḥ, miserliness, and meanness are related; shuḥḥ combines stinginess with greed, and in religious law means withholding what is obligatory.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r4.anchor: والشح والبخل واللؤم نظائر، والشح: بخل مع حرص

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r5.claim: يوق is jussive as the verb in a conditional, marked by loss of the original alif; شح is accusative as the object, and the stated subject stands for an implicit agent.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r5.anchor: يوق جزم؛ لأنه مجازاة، وعلامة الجزم ذهاب الألف

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r6.claim: One account says the verse came when Muslims asked for the property of Banu Nadir after their expulsion; the property was left to the Prophet to distribute as he chose.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r6.anchor: قيل: لما خرج بنو النضير من ديارهم، سأل المسلمون قسمة أموالهم، فنزلت الآية، وجعل ذلك لرسول الله

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r7.claim: Another account says the Prophet offered the Ansar either a share of the fay while emigrants remained in their homes or the whole share for the emigrants; they chose the latter and housed them, prompting the verse.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r7.anchor: فنادوا كلهم من كل جانب أن تقسمها بينهم ويكونون في بيوتنا ودورنا كما كانوا، فأعطاهم الفيء

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r8.claim: Anas ibn Malik reports that an Ansari household passed a roasted sheep's head from one hungrier person to another until seven people had shared it.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r8.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في أهل بيت من الأنصار كان لهم رأس غنم مشوي، فأهدوا إلى غيرهم

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r9.claim: Another account tells of seven thirsty men at Uhud who passed around enough water for one person; none drank and they died, and God praised them.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r9.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في سبعة عطشوا يوم أحد، فجاء بماء يكفي لأحدهم، فقال أحدهم: ناول فلانا

JISHUMI:v9p6847/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r10.claim: A hungry visitor was hosted by an Ansari whose family had only food for their children; the couple pretended to eat while letting the guest eat and their children sleep hungry, and the verse was revealed about them.
JISHUMI:v9p6847/r10.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في قصة رجل جاء إلى رسول الله

BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r8.claim: The new clause praises the Ansar, including their love for the emigrants and their complete acceptance of the emigrants receiving the spoils.
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r8.anchor: كلام مستأنف مسوق لمدح الأنصار بخصال حميدة من جملتها محبتهم للمهاجرين

BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r9.claim: The Ansar are the Aws and Khazraj, traced through their forebears to the Azd and Qahtan, whom the source identifies as the origin of the pure Arabs.
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r9.anchor: والأنصار بنو الأوس والخزرج ابني حارثة بن ثعلبة بن عمرو بن عامر بن حارثة ابن امرىء القيس

BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r10.claim: Ghassan is linked to a spring near al-Juhfa where a group descended from the Azd settled and drank, taking their name from it.
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r10.anchor: ومن الأنصار غسان كشداد ماء قرب الجحفة نزل عليه قوم من ولد الأزد فشربوا منه فنسبوا إليه

BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r11.claim: The root sense of bawāʾ is parts being level or fitting together in a place, unlike nubuww, which is being ill-fitted; a place is bawāʾ when it suits its occupant.
BURSEVI:v9p350#2/r11.anchor: وأصل البواء مساواة الأجزاء في المكان خلاف النبو الذي هو منافاة الأجزاء يقال مكان بواء إذا لم يكن نابيا بنازله

BURSEVI:v9p351/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r1.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p351/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet chose a settled place for relieving himself as he would for his residence.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r1.anchor: وروي إنه عليه السلام كان يتبوأ لبوله كما يتبوأ لمنزله

BURSEVI:v9p351/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r2.claim: Tabawwaʾū means taking a place as a home and settling there; since faith is not a physical place, several figurative parses are offered.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r2.anchor: وتبوأوا لمنزل اتخاذه منزلا والتمكن والاستقرار فيه فالمتبوأ فيه لا بد أن يكون من قبيل المنازل والأمكنة

BURSEVI:v9p351/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r3.claim: Possible constructions treat the state as a place, include adherence in the verb, or understand “they took the abode and embraced, accepted, or preferred faith,” with a verb omitted by ellipsis.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r3.anchor: وقيل ضمن التبوؤ معنى اللزوم وقيل تبوأوا الدار وأخلصوا الإيمان أو قبلوه أو آثروه

BURSEVI:v9p351/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r4.claim: Bursevi suggests the original sense was “the abode of faith”: Medina is faith’s home and the home of migration, while the conjunction explicitly praises their faith because residence alone is insufficient.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r4.anchor: لعل أصل الكلام والذين تبوأوا دار الإيمان فإن المدينة يقال لها دار الإيمان

BURSEVI:v9p351/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r5.claim: “Before them” means before the emigrants’ migration, with an omitted noun understood; the Ansar did not all believe before the emigrants, since some believed before the Hijra and others after.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r5.anchor: أي من قبل هجرة المهاجرين فقدر المضاف لأن الأنصار لم يؤمنوا قبل

BURSEVI:v9p351/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p351/r6.claim: One commentator says the Ansar in their homeland embraced Islam and built mosques two years before the Prophet’s arrival.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم مراد أنصار ندكه درديار خود ايمان آوردند وبد وسال يش ازقدوم حضرت مساجد ساختند

BURSEVI:v9p351/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r7.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v9p351/r7.claim: Al-Irshad reads making faith one’s home as adhering to it and fulfilling all its rights, including public rites; the Ansar preceded the emigrants in public practice, not in inward sincerity.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r7.anchor: قال في الإرشاد : يجوز أن يجعل اتخاذ الإيمان مباءة ولزومه وإخلاصه عبارة عن إقامة كافة حقوقه

BURSEVI:v9p351/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r8.claim: The inward reading makes the abode the heart, home of truth and sincerity, and faith a special, God-given faith established within it.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r8.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى دار القلب التي هي دار الصدق والإخلاص وإلى الإيمان الاختصاصي الوهبي بتحقيقه وتثبيته

BURSEVI:v9p351/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r9.claim: The Ansar love emigrants for migrating out of love for faith, and because God and His beloved love them; the beloved’s beloved is beloved.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r9.anchor: يحبونهم من حيث مهاجرتهم إليهم لمحبتهم الإيمان ولأن الله وحبيبه أحباهم وحبيب الحبيب حبيب

BURSEVI:v9p351/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r10.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v9p351/r10.claim: Kashf al-Asrar takes the phrase as an allusion to the Ansar’s hospitality toward guests.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r10.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار كنايتست از مهمان دوستى أنصار

BURSEVI:v9p351/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r11.claim: Hajah means something one needs; the phrase denies that the Ansar felt a need or desire for what the emigrants received in spoils and other gifts.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r11.anchor: وغيره ومن بيانية يقال خذ منه حاجتك

BURSEVI:v9p351/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r12.claim: Negating that they found such a need in themselves is more emphatic than saying they knew of none; another reading denies their desire for the gifts, and another denies resentment or envy.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r12.anchor: والمراد من نفي الوجدان نفي العلم لأن الوجدان في النفس إدراك علمي وفيه من المبالغة ما ليس في يعلمون

BURSEVI:v9p351/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r13.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p351/r13.claim: Al-Raghib defines need as dependence on something together with desire for it.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r13.anchor: قال الراغب الحاجة إلى الشيء الفقر إليه مع محبته

BURSEVI:v9p351/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r14.claim: The verb means they prefer the emigrants, with its object omitted; they put them first in all means of livelihood.

BURSEVI:v9p351/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r15.claim: Their generosity could mean a man with two wives giving one up so an emigrant could marry her.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r15.anchor: حتى أن من كان عنده امرأتان كان ينزل عن إحداهما ويزوجها واحدا منهم

BURSEVI:v9p351/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351/r16.claim: Ithar means giving another something that you yourself need.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r16.anchor: والإيثار عطاؤك ما أنت تحتاج إليه

BURSEVI:v9p351/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351/r17.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p351/r17.claim: The Prophet says every gathering has included both generous and miserly people except the Ansar, who were all generous and had no miser among them.
BURSEVI:v9p351/r17.anchor: وفي الخبر لم يجتمع في الدنيا قوم قط إلا وفيهم أسخياء وبخلاء إلا في الأنصار فإن كلهم أسخياء ما فيهم من بخيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r1.claim: Those who settled the abode are the Anṣār, and the phrase is coordinated with the Muhājirūn.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r2.claim: The coordination of faith with the abode can mean they settled the city and sincerely embraced faith, as in the cited coordination of unlike objects.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r3.claim: Alternatively, they made faith a settled home because they were firmly rooted and steadfast in it, just as they settled in the city.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r3.anchor: وجعلوا الإيمان مستقرا ومتوطنا لهم لتمكنهم منه واستقامتهم عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r4.claim: Alternatively, “the abode” means the abode of migration and faith: the definite article stands for a possessive construction, with “abode” elided from “abode of faith.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r4.anchor: أراد دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان ، فأقام لام التعريف في الدار مقام المضاف إليه ، وحذف المضاف من دار الإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r5.claim: Alternatively, Medina itself is called faith because it is the abode of migration and the place where faith appeared.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r5.anchor: أو سمى المدينة لأنها دار الهجرة ومكان ظهور الإيمان بالإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r6.claim: “Before them” means before the Muhājirūn, because the Anṣār settled the abode of migration and faith first; another view takes it as before their migration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r6.anchor: من قبل المهاجرين ؛ لأنهم سبقوهم في تبوىء دار الهجرة والإيمان . وقيل : من قبل هجرتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r7.claim: Lā yajidūn means they do not find or know within themselves; ḥājah is a desired need for any of the spoils given to the migrants, and their hearts do not covet it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r7.anchor: ولا يعلمون في أنفسهم { حاجة مما أوتوا } أي طلب محتاج إليه مما أوتي المهاجرون من الفيء وغيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r8.claim: A needed thing is called a ḥājah, as in telling someone to take his need or giving him the amount he needs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r8.anchor: والمحتاج إليه يسمى حاجة ؛ يقال : خذ منه حاجتك ، وأعطاه من ماله حاجته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r9.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r9.claim: The Prophet distributed Banū Naḍīr's property among the Muhājirūn, except for three needy Anṣār; he offered the Anṣār a choice, and they chose to share homes and property and prefer the migrants in the spoils.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r9.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم أموال بني النضير على المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار إلا ثلاثة نفر محتاجين : أبادجانة سماك بن خرشة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r10.claim: Khaṣāṣah means need or poverty, originally referring to gaps in a house; the clause is circumstantial, assuming their poverty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r10.anchor: أي خلة ، وأصلها : خصاص البيت ، وهي فروجه ؛ والجملة في موضع الحال ، أي : مفروضة خصاصتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r11.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r11.claim: Shuḥḥ is read with either ḍamma or kasra on the shīn.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r12.claim: Shuḥḥ is meanness: a soul's tight, greedy resistance to giving, as illustrated by the cited line.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p504/r12.anchor: اللؤم ، وأن تكون نفس الرجل كزة حريصة على المنع

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r1.claim: Khasāṣa means need or want; its root evokes gaps in a house, likening poverty to an enclosure with openings that cannot meet its needs.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r1.anchor: أصلها خصاص البيت وهي فرجة شبه حالة الفقر والحاجة

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib says unfillable poverty is called khasāṣa, as it is also called khalla; a khas is a reed-and-branch hut named for its gaps.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r2.anchor: قال الراغب عبر عن الفقر الذي لا يسد بالخصاصة كما عبر عنه بالخلة والخص بيت من قصب وشجر

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r3.claim: The Prophet distributed Banū Naḍīr property among the Emigrants, except for three needy Ansār: Abū Dujāna, Sahl b. Ḥunayf, and al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣimma.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r3.anchor: وكان عليه السلام قسم أموال بني النضير على المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار إلا ثلاثة نفر محتاجين

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r4.claim: An alternate report says only Sahl and Abū Dujāna received shares, since al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣimma had died at Biʾr Maʿūna.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r4.anchor: وروي لم يعط إلا رجلين سهلا وأبا دجانة فإن الحارث بن الصمة قتل في بئر معونة

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r5.claim: The Prophet offered the Ansār a choice of sharing their homes and wealth with the Emigrants and sharing the spoils, or keeping their property without a share; they chose to give their property and the spoils to the Emigrants.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r5.anchor: فقالت : الأنصار بل نقسم لهم من أموالنا وديارنا ونؤثرهم بالغنيمة

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r6.claim: The Prophet kept some land for his own cultivation and later had the Emigrants return the palm groves the Ansār had lent them for their fruit, since the Ansār no longer needed them and had never transferred ownership.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r6.anchor: وكان عليه السلام أعطى بعض الأراضي وأبقى بعضها يزرع له ولما أعطى المهاجرين أمرهم برد ما كان للأنصار

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r7.speaker: أنس رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r7.claim: An Anṣārī in hardship received a sheep's head and passed it among seven households, each considering a neighbor more needy, until it returned to him.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r7.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : أهدي لرجل من الأنصار رأس شاة وكان مجهودا

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r8.speaker: حذيفة العدوي
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r8.claim: At Yarmūk, Ḥudhayfa al-ʿAdawī offered water to his wounded cousin; the cousin directed him to Hishām b. al-ʿĀṣ, who passed him to another wounded man, and all three died before drinking.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r8.anchor: قال حذيفة العدوي انطلقت يوم اليرموك أطلب ابن عم لي ومعي شيء من الماء

BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r9.claim: Giving up one's own life for another is a form of self-preference and exceeds preferring another with one's wealth.
BURSEVI:v9p351#2/r9.anchor: وهذا من قبيل الإيثار بالنفس وهو فوق الإيثار بالمال

BURSEVI:v9p353/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p353/r1.claim: Shuḥḥ combines miserliness with greed, two blameworthy traits of the self; it is attributed to the self because it is an innate impulse toward withholding.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r1.anchor: والشح بالضم والكسر بخل مع حرص فيكون جامعا بين ذميمتين من صفات النفس وإضافته إلى النفس لأنه غريزة فيها

BURSEVI:v9p353/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p353/r2.claim: Being protected from one's avarice by God's enabling means resisting the self's love of wealth and aversion to spending.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r2.anchor: أي ومن يوق بتوفيق الله شحها حتى يخالفها فيما يغلب عليها من حب المال وبغض الإنفاق

BURSEVI:v9p353/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p353/r3.claim: The successful are those who attain every desired good and escape every harm; falāḥ is happiness in both abodes.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r3.anchor: الفائزون بكل مطلوب الناجون من كل مكروه والفلاح اسم لسعادة الدارين

BURSEVI:v9p353/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p353/r4.claim: The success clause is an aside praising the Ansār, since the qualities just described are their virtues and refined states.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r4.anchor: والجملة اعتراض وارد لمدح الأنصار والثناء عليهم فإن الفتوى هي الأوصاف المذكورة في حقهم

BURSEVI:v9p353/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p353/r5.claim: The Prophet called love of the Ansār a sign of faith and hatred of them a sign of hypocrisy.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r5.anchor: قال عليه السلام : آية الإيمان حب الأنصار وآية النفاق بغض الأنصار

BURSEVI:v9p353/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p353/r6.claim: The Prophet prayed that God forgive the Ansār, their children, and their grandchildren.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r6.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : اللهم اغفر للأنصار ولأبناء الأنصار وأبناء أبناء الأنصار

BURSEVI:v9p353/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r7.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v9p353/r7.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says innate generosity opposes avarice, which is among the self's inherent traits; God promises success to the person who spends and gives.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r7.anchor: قال السهروردي في العوارف : السخاء صفة غريزية في مقابلة الشح والشح من لوازم صفة النفس

BURSEVI:v9p353/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p353/r8.claim: The Prophet counted obedient avarice among three ruinous traits: avarice is destructive when obeyed, while its mere presence is natural to the earthly self.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r8.anchor: والنبي عليه السلام نبه بقوله ثلاث مهلكات وثلاث منجيات فجعل إحدى المهلكات شحا مطاعا

BURSEVI:v9p353/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r9.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v9p353/r9.claim: Al-Suhrawardī distinguishes innate sakha from acquired jud: every innately generous person gives generously, but not every generous giver has sakha; Sufis' sakha prompts giving and altruism.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r9.anchor: والسخاء أتم وأكمل من الجود وفي مقابلة الجود البخل وفي مقابلة السخاء الشح

BURSEVI:v9p353/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r10.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v9p353/r10.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says God is not described by sakha, which arises from innate dispositions; acquired generosity may seek display or reward, while true sakha is free of recompense and belongs to the people of purity.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r10.anchor: والحق تعالى لا يوصف بالسخاء لأن السخاء من نتيجة الغرائز والله تعالى منزه عن الغريزة

BURSEVI:v9p353/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r11.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v9p353/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says shuḥḥ means committing sins, as though one were miserly with obedience.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن رحمه الله : الشح هو العمل بالمعاصي كأنه يشح بالطاعة

BURSEVI:v9p353/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p353/r12.claim: Another definition of shuḥḥ is letting one's gaze covet what does not belong to oneself.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r12.anchor: فدخل فيه ما قيل الشح أن تطمح عين الرجل إلى ما ليس له

BURSEVI:v9p353/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p353/r13.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p353/r13.claim: The Prophet described looking at another man's woman as shuḥḥ; the source links it to withholding the gaze and chastity and says such a person does not prosper.
BURSEVI:v9p353/r13.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : من الشح نظرك إلى امرأة غيرك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r6.claim: One syntactic reading uses fronting and postponement: they settled the abode before the emigrants and had embraced faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r6.anchor: ويكون على التقديم والتأخير ومعناه تبوءوا الدار من قبلهم والإيمان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r7.claim: On the surface reading, they had settled the abode and faith before the emigrants came, welcoming and supporting them with homes and wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r7.anchor: الثاني : أن الكلام على ظاهره ومعناه أنهم تبوءوا الدار والإيمان قبل الهجرة إليهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r8.claim: Not finding need in their hearts may mean having no jealousy or envy over the emigrants' preference and closeness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r8.anchor: أحدهما : غيرة وحسدا على ما قدموا به من تفضيل وتقريب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r9.claim: Hasan specifies that they did not envy the emigrants for the property of the spoils and other wealth allotted to them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r9.anchor: الثاني : يعني حسدا على ما خصوا به من مال الفيء وغيره فلا يحسدونهم عليه , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r10.claim: They put the emigrants first even when they themselves faced poverty and need.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p504#2/r10.anchor: يعني يفضلونهم ويقدمونهم على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم فاقة وحاجة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r1.claim: The cited verse uses khisasa for poverty and need; the poem says the sickly prosper when spring arrives.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن حيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r2.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Hayyan say the Ansar preferred the emigrants in the fay and booty allotted to them, despite their own need.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r3.claim: An unnamed report says that after the Prophet allocated Banu al-Nadir's fay and Qurayza's spoils to the emigrants, the Ansar offered their own property and chose that the emigrants receive the fay; the verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r3.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم على المهاجرين ما أفاء الله من النضير ونفل من قريظة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Ansar preferred the emigrants by giving them their own wealth and sharing it with them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r4.anchor: الثاني : أنهم آثروا المهاجرين بأموالهم وواسوهم بها . روى ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r5.claim: In Ibn Zayd's report, the Ansar offered divided estates; the Prophet proposed caring for the emigrants, who could not work, and sharing dates from Banu al-Nadir's palms, and they agreed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r5.anchor: روى ابن زيد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r6.speaker: ابن جريج وطاووس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Tawus define soul's avarice as wanting wealth in other people's hands for oneself without being content.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r6.anchor: أن يشح بما في أيدي الناس يحب أن يكون له ولا يقنع , قاله ابن جريج وطاووس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r7.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r7.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets it as withholding zakat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r7.anchor: أنه منع الزكاة ، قاله ابن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is the soul's desire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r8.anchor: يعني هوى نفسه ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r9.claim: Ibn Masud defines the Quranic avarice as acquiring forbidden wealth, specifically consuming another person's property unjustly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r9.anchor: إنما الشح الذي ذكره الله في القرآن أن تأكل مال أخيك ظلما ولكن ذلك البخل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r10.claim: Al-Aswad reports a man feared damnation because he was too stingy to give; Ibn Masud answered that ordinary miserliness is not the Quranic avarice, which is wrongful appropriation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r11.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r11.claim: Ata interprets it as withholding expenditure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r11.anchor: أنه الإمساك عن النفقة , قاله عطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r12.speaker: ابن عيينة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r12.claim: Ibn Uyayna interprets it as injustice.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r13.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r13.claim: Hasan understands it as acting on one's desire to disobey God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r13.anchor: أنه أراد العمل بمعاصي الله , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r14.speaker: الليث
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r14.claim: Al-Layth says it means abandoning obligations and violating prohibitions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r14.anchor: أنه أراد ترك الفرائض وانتهاك المحارم , قاله الليث

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r15.claim: One view says shuhh and bukhl mean the same thing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r16.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r16.claim: Ibn Masud distinguishes them: shuhh is taking wealth without right, while bukhl is withholding what is due.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r16.anchor: قاله ابن مسعود . الثاني : أن الشح بما في يدي غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r17.speaker: طاووس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r17.claim: Tawus distinguishes them by ownership: shuhh covets another's property, while bukhl concerns one's own.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p506/r17.anchor: قاله طاووس . { والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا }

MUJAHID:v2p664/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p664/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p664/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies those who settled in the abode and faith before the emigrants as the Anṣār.
MUJAHID:v2p664/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ والذين تبوؤوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم ﴾ وهم الأنصار ﴿ من قبلهم ﴾ من قبل المهاجرين

MUJAHID:v2p664/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p664/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p664/r2.claim: Mujahid explains before them as before the emigrants.
MUJAHID:v2p664/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ والذين تبوؤوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم ﴾ وهم الأنصار ﴿ من قبلهم ﴾ من قبل المهاجرين

MUJAHID:v2p664/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p664/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p664/r3.claim: Mujahid says the Anṣār showed generosity when the booty was withheld from them, preferring the emigrants although none of that booty went to the Anṣār.
MUJAHID:v2p664/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ والذين تبوؤوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم ﴾ وهم الأنصار ﴿ من قبلهم ﴾ من قبل المهاجرين ثم نعت سخاوة أنفسهم

MUJAHID:v2p664/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p664/r4.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p664/r4.anchor: عن الحسن ﴿ ولو كان بهم خصاصة ﴾ يعني فاقة

MUQATIL:59:9/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r1.claim: The Ansar settled in Medina years before the believers migrated to them.
MUQATIL:59:9/r1.anchor: يعني أوطنوا دار المدينة من قبل هجرة المؤمنين، إليهم بسنين

MUQATIL:59:9/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r2.claim: The Ansar had faith before the migration of the Muhajirun.
MUQATIL:59:9/r2.anchor: ثم قال: { والإيمان من قبلهم } من قبل هجرة المهاجرين، ثم قال: للأنصار:

MUQATIL:59:9/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r3.claim: The Ansar love the believers who migrated to them.
MUQATIL:59:9/r3.anchor: للأنصار: { يحبون من هاجر إليهم } من المؤمنين { ولا يجدون في صدورهم } يعني قلوبهم

MUQATIL:59:9/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r4.claim: They hold no resentment in their hearts about the booty given to their Muhajirun brothers.
MUQATIL:59:9/r4.anchor: { ولا يجدون في صدورهم } يعني قلوبهم { حاجة مما أوتوا } يعني مما أعطى إخوانهم المهاجرين من الفىء

MUQATIL:59:9/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r5.claim: Even while needy, the Ansar preferred the Muhajirun by giving them the booty rather than keeping it for themselves.
MUQATIL:59:9/r5.anchor: يقول: لا تضيق { ولو كان بهم خصاصة } يعني الفاقة فآثروا المهاجرين بالفىء على أنفسهم

MUQATIL:59:9/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r6.claim: Being protected from the soul's avarice means that God shields a person from its greed; this describes the Ansar willingly foregoing the booty.
MUQATIL:59:9/r6.anchor: ثم قال: { ومن يوق شح نفسه } يعني ومن يقيه الله حرص نفسه، سعنى الأنصار حين طابت أنفسهم عن الفىء لإخوانهم

MUQATIL:59:9/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:9/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:9/r7.claim: The Muhajirun and Ansar are the first two groups; the remaining group is the Successors who entered Islam afterward through the end of time.
MUQATIL:59:9/r7.anchor: فقد ذهب صنفان المهاجرون والأنصار وبقي صنف واحد، وهم التابعون الذين دخلوا في الإسلام إلى يوم القيامة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r1.claim: The clause is coordinated with “the Emigrants”; it refers to the Anṣār.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r3.claim: One reading is that they sincerely embraced faith, with ellipsis as in the poetic phrase “I fed her straw and cold water.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r3.anchor: وأخلصوا الايمان كقوله علفتها تبنا وماء باردا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, they made faith a settled home, being firmly established and steadfast in it as they were settled in Medina.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r4.anchor: أو وجعلوا الايمان مستقرا ومتوطنا لهم لتمكنهم واستقامتهم عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, “the abode” means the Abode of Emigration, with the definite article standing for a possessive phrase and “settled” elided before “faith.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r5.anchor: أو أراد دار الهجرة فاقام لام التعريف في الدار مقام المضاف اليه وحذف تبوئ دار الهجرة والايمان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r6.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r6.claim: A further reported interpretation takes “before them” as before the Emigrants' migration.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r7.claim: The Anṣār loved the Emigrants so much that they shared their wealth and homes; a man with two wives even gave one up for an Emigrant to marry.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r7.anchor: حتى شاطروهم أموالهم وأنزلوهم منازلهم ونزل من كانت له امرأتان عن احداهما حتى تزوج بها رجل من المهاجرين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r8.claim: They did not covet what the Emigrants received from the spoils or elsewhere: their souls neither pursued nor desired any of it as something they needed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r8.anchor: يعني ان نفوسهم لم تتبع ما أعطوا ولم تطمح إلى شيء منه تحتاج اليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r9.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r9.claim: One view glosses “need” as envy of the spoils allotted to the Emigrants.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r9.anchor: وقيل حاجة حسدا مما أعطي المهاجرون من الفيء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r10.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r10.claim: Another view understands distress over what they themselves missed, with two possessive phrases elided.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r10.anchor: وقيل 4 لا يجدون في صدورهم من حاجة من فقد ما أوتوا فحذف المضافان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r11.claim: They put others before themselves even when poor; the clause describes their state, supposing their poverty.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r11.anchor: فقر وأصلها خصاص البيت وهى فروجه والجملة في موضع الحال أي مفروضة خصاصتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r12.claim: A report tells of an Anṣārī host putting his children to sleep, serving a guest, and extinguishing the lamp so the guest could eat while he went without.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r12.anchor: روى أنه نزل برجل منهم ضيف فنوم الصبية وقرب الطعام وأطفأ المصباح ليشبع ضيفه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r13.speaker: أنس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r13.claim: Anas reports that a roasted head passed among nine needy people, each sending it to a neighbor, until it returned to the first.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r13.anchor: وعن أنس أهدى لبعضهم رأس مشوي وهو مجهود فوجهه إلى جاره فتداولته تسعة أنفس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r14.speaker: أبو زيد
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r14.claim: Abū Zayd contrasts a youth from Balkh: their asceticism is to endure lack and give others preference when they have food, unlike merely eating when they find it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r14.anchor: أبو زيد قال لي شاب من أهل بلخ با الزهد عندكم قلت إذا وجدنا أكلنا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r15.claim: Shuḥ is a miserly, tight-fisted self eager to withhold; those protected from it attain what they seek.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r15.anchor: والشح أكل اللؤم وأن تكون نفس الرجل كزة حريصه على المنع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r16.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r16.claim: Another distinction says shuḥ is wrongful consumption of a brother's wealth, while bukhl is withholding one's own.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r16.anchor: وقيل الشح أكل مال أخيك ظلما والبخل منع مالك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r17.speaker: كسرى
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r17.claim: Kisrā says avarice is worse than poverty: the poor can recover when wealth comes, unlike the miser.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p231#2/r17.anchor: وعن كسرى الشح أضر من الفقر لآن الفقير يتسع إذا وجد بخلاف الشحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r1.claim: There is no disagreement that those who settled the abode are the Ansar, who established themselves in Medina before the emigrants.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r1.anchor: لا خلاف أن الذين تبوءوا الدار هم الأنصار الذين استوطنوا المدينة قبل المهاجرين إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r2.claim: Al-īmān is accusative under a verb other than tabawwaʾ, since settlement applies to places; min qablihim attaches to tabawwaʾ and means before the emigrants.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r2.anchor: «والإيمان» نصب بفعل غير تبوأ لأن التبوء إنما يكون في الأماكن.

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r3.claim: The verse says the Ansar settled Medina and sincerely embraced faith before the Prophet’s migration to them, not that they believed before the emigrants did.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r3.anchor: والمعنى: والذين تبوءوا الدار من قبل المهاجرين واعتقدوا الإيمان وأخلصوه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r4.speaker: أبو علي والزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r4.claim: One grammatical explanation coordinates faith with an implied command, like “gather your affair and your partners,” meaning summon the partners.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r4.anchor: أي وادعوا شركاءهم ذكره أبو علي والزمخشري وغيرهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r5.claim: Other analyses supply omitted places of faith, understand the Ansar as adhering to home and faith, or treat settling faith as metaphor.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r5.anchor: ويجوز حمله على حذف المضاف كأنه قال: تبوءوا الدار ومواضع الإيمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r6.claim: Tabawwaʾ means to become established and settled.

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r7.claim: The author rejects reading this verse as coordinated with the preceding verse about poor emigrants: the earlier verses discuss Banu Nadir and the distinct allocation of their fay.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r7.anchor: ولو تأملوا ذلك وأنصفوا لوجدوه على خلاف ما ذهبوا إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r8.claim: The author treats 59:9 as a new beginning praising the Ansar, who yielded the fay to emigrants without envy; 59:10 also begins a new sentence.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r8.anchor: ابتداء كلام في مدح الأنصار والثناء عليهم فإنهم سلموا ذلك الفيء للمهاجرين

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r9.speaker: إسماعيل بن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r9.claim: Ismail ibn Ishaq instead coordinates the Ansar and later arrivals with the preceding passage, making emigrants and Ansar partners in the fay.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r9.anchor: وقال إسماعيل ابن إسحاق: إن قوله { والذين تبوءوا الدار }

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r10.speaker: مالك بن أوس وعمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r10.claim: The segment begins a report that Malik ibn Aws heard Umar recite this verse, but gives no further content here.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9/r10.anchor: وقال مالك بن أوس: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r1.claim: A report describes Umar reciting the charity, booty, and fayʾ passages, then saying even a shepherd in remote Himyar would receive his share without labor.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r1.anchor: لئن عشت ليأتين الراعي وهو بسرو حمير نصيبه منها لم يعرق فيها جبينه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r2.claim: Another account says Umar consulted the Muhajirun and Ansar, then concluded that the later-Muslim verse included every Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنه دعا المهاجرين والأنصار واستشارهم فيما فتح الله عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r3.speaker: عمر
