QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r3.claim: Umar retained the conquered lands of Iraq and Egypt, with their revenues supporting fighters, dependants, and their families; Zubayr, Bilal, and others urged him to distribute them.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r3.anchor: أن عمر أبقى سواد العراق ومصر وما ظهر عليه من الغنائم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r4.claim: One account says Umar first sought the army's consent, buying out those who refused; Qurtubi says consensual purchase or relinquishment made this equivalent to the Prophet's division of Khaybar.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r4.anchor: فمن رضي له بترك حظه بغير ثمن ليبقيه للمسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r5.claim: Other accounts say Umar kept the land without compensating the army, or interpreted the fayʾ verses through the later groups named in 59:8–10.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: إنه أبقاها بغير شيء أعطاه أهل الجيوش

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r6.claim: Malik allows the imam to hold conquered real estate for the interests of the Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r6.anchor: فقال مالك: للإمام أن يوقفها لمصالح المسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa gives the imam a choice between distributing conquered land and holding it for Muslim interests.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة الإمام مخير بين أن يقسمها أو يجعلها وقفا

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r8.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r8.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says the imam must distribute conquered land unless its owners freely agree to its dedication; those who do not consent retain their property, and Umar obtained consent and bought shares.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r8.anchor: وقال الشافعي: ليس للإمام حبسها عنهم بغير رضاهم، بل يقسمها عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r10.claim: Malik praised Medina because it was settled through faith and migration, unlike other towns conquered by force, and cited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#2/r10.anchor: فقال: إن المدينة تبوئت بالإيمان والهجرة، وإن غيرها من القرى افتتحت بالسيف

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r1.claim: The phrase means the Ansar did not envy the Muhajirun for the fayʾ and other property allotted to them, as commentators generally explain it.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r1.anchor: يعني لا يحسدون المهاجرين على ما خصوا به من مال الفيء وغيره كذلك قال الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a host who had only his children's ration, put them to bed and extinguished the lamp to feed a guest; the verse was revealed about this act. Tirmidhi grades the report sound and authentic, and Muslim also records it.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r2.anchor: في الترمذي عن أبي هريرة: أن رجلا بات به ضيف فلم يكن عنده إلا قوته وقوت صبيانه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r3.claim: The construction ellipses two nouns: its sense is that they felt no distress at lacking what the Muhajirun received.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r3.anchor: وفيه تقدير حذف مضافين المعنى مس حاجة من فقد ما أوتوا

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r4.claim: Anything a person feels in the heart that needs to be removed can be called a need or distress.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r4.anchor: وكل ما يجد الإنسان في صدره مما يحتاج إلى إزالته فهو حاجة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r5.claim: When Banu Nadir's property was gained, the Prophet thanked the Ansar for housing and sharing wealth with the Muhajirun, then offered either a joint allotment while they stayed or an allotment to the Muhajirun who would leave.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r5.anchor: إن أحببتم قسمت ما أفاء الله علي من بني النضير بينكم وبينهم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r6.speaker: سعد بن عبادة، سعد بن معاذ
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r6.claim: Saʿd ibn ʿUbada and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh chose the fayʾ for the Muhajirun while keeping them in the Ansar's homes; the Ansar consented and the Prophet prayed for mercy upon them and their children.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r6.anchor: فقال سعد بن عبادة وسعد بن معاذ: بل نقسمه بين المهاجرين

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r7.claim: The Prophet gave the Banu Nadir property to the Muhajirun and gave nothing to the Ansar except three men mentioned earlier in the commentary.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r7.anchor: وأعطى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار شيئا إلا الثلاثة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r8.claim: Alternatively, the verse may mean they felt no resentment about what was given even if the amount was small, but remained content with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r8.anchor: إذا كان قليلا بل يقنعون به ويرضون عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r9.claim: The Prophet warned the Ansar that they would later see others favored over them and told them to be patient until they met him at the Pool.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#3/r9.anchor: سترون بعدي أثرة فاصبروا حتى تلقوني على الحوض

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r1.claim: In another Abu Hurayra report, the Prophet sought a host for a destitute visitor; an Ansari and his wife pretended to eat while giving the guest their children's food, and God marveled at their act.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r1.anchor: جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني مجهود

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r2.claim: A variant names the Ansari host as Abu Talha and says the verse was revealed after the guest was served the household's food.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r2.anchor: وفي رواية عن أبي هريرة قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r3.claim: Al-Mahdawi attributes the occasion to Thabit ibn Qays staying with Abu al-Mutawakkil, who had only enough food for his children and gave it to his guest.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r3.anchor: وذكر المهدوي عن أبي هريرة أن هذا نزل في ثابت بن قيس

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas likewise reports that Thabit ibn Qays was hosted by Abu al-Mutawakkil, who put the children to sleep and served their food to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r4.anchor: وكذا ذكر النحاس قال: قال أبو هريرة: نزل برجل من الأنصار يقال له أبو المتوكل

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar's account says a Companion passed a sheep's head to a needier household; it circulated through seven homes and returned to its first recipient, occasioning the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: أهدي لرجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأس شاة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r6.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits from Anas a similar story: a needy Companion sent a sheep's head through seven households, and it returned to him before the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#4/r6.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي عن أنس قال: أهدى لرجل من الصحابة رأس شاة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that on Banu Nadir day the Prophet offered the Ansar a choice: share their homes and wealth with the Muhajirun and share the booty, or keep their property and receive none; they chose to share and prefer the Muhajirun, and the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r1.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للأنصار يوم بني النضير: «إن شئتم قسمت للمهاجرين من دياركم وأموالكم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r2.claim: Qurtubi judges the earlier guest-hosting account of the occasion of revelation more authentic than the preceding alternative account.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r2.anchor: والأول أصح. وفي الصحيحين عن أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r3.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r3.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Anas reports that a man had given the Prophet date palms, which the Prophet returned to him after the conquests of Qurayza and Banu Nadir.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أنس: أن الرجل كان يجعل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم النخلات

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r4.speaker: الزهري عن أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r4.claim: The Muhajirun arrived in Medina with nothing; the landowning Ansar shared half their annual fruit and undertook the work and expenses. Umm Sulaym had given the Prophet date palms, which he gave to Umm Ayman.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#5/r4.anchor: لما قدم المهاجرون من مكة إلى المدينة قدموا وليس بأيديهم شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r1.claim: Ithar is preferring another over oneself and worldly interests for religious benefit; it grows from firm certainty, deep love, and patience in hardship. The implied object is the Muhajirun, favored with wealth and homes despite the Ansar's own need.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r1.anchor: الإيثار: هو تقديم الغير على النفس وحظوظها الدنياوية، ورغبة في الحظوظ الدينية

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r2.claim: The verb's omitted object is the Muhajirun: the Ansar preferred them in wealth and dwellings despite needing those things themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r2.anchor: ومفعول الإيثار محذوف أي يؤثرونهم على أنفسهم بأموالهم ومنازلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r3.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r3.claim: Malik's Muwatta says, in a report reaching him from ʿAʾisha, that she gave her only loaf to a fasting beggar; a sheep wrapped in dough was later gifted to her, and she said that was better than her loaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r3.anchor: أنه بلغه عن عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن مسكينا سألها وهي صائمة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r4.claim: Scholars call ʿAʾisha's gift profitable wealth and a virtuous deed whose reward God may hasten without diminishing what is stored; whoever gives something for God will not miss it, and she exemplified the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r4.anchor: قال علماؤنا: هذا من المال الرابح، والفعل الزاكي عند الله تعالى يعجل منه ما يشاء

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r5.claim: The phrase 'a sheep and its wrapping' refers to a regional delicacy: a slaughtered sheep was covered in wheat dough and baked in a tannur so its drippings stayed in the casing.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r5.anchor: كان هذا من طعامهم، يأتون إلى الشاة أو الخروف إذا سلخوه غطوه كله بعجين البر

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r6.claim: Nafiʿ reports that Ibn ʿUmar repeatedly gave a grape cluster he had bought for a sick person to a beggar, though someone kept buying it back; he would not have eaten it had he known it was the same cluster, since charity should not be taken back.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#6/r6.anchor: وروى النسائي عن نافع أن ابن عمر اشتكى واشتهى عنبا

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r1.speaker: مالك الدار
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r1.claim: Continuing the report transmitted by Ibn al-Mubarak from Malik al-Dar, Abu Ubayda and Muʿadh each redistributed Umar's 400-dinar gifts among needy households; Umar rejoiced that they were brothers like one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r1.anchor: فرجع الغلام إلى عمر، فأخبره فوجده قد أعد مثلها لمعاذ بن جبل

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r2.claim: Qurtubi also mentions that Muʿawiya gave ʿAʾisha ten thousand and that al-Munkadir came in to her.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r2.anchor: ونحوه عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في إعطاء معاوية إياها، وكان عشرة آلاف

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r3.claim: Reports against giving away all one's property apply to those unlikely to endure poverty and at risk of begging; the Ansar could bear hardship, so giving was better for them, while restraint suits those who cannot endure it.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r3.anchor: إنما كره ذلك في حق من لا يوثق منه الصبر على الفقر

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r4.claim: A man brought a gold piece as charity, and the Prophet rebuked giving away everything and then sitting to beg from people.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r4.anchor: يأتي أحدكم بجميع ما يملكه فيتصدق به ثم يقعد يتكفف الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r5.claim: Giving one's life is a higher form of altruism than giving wealth, and Sufi formulations define love as preferring the beloved over oneself; the wife of al-ʿAziz did so for Joseph.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r5.anchor: ومن عبارات الصوفية الرشيقة في حد المحبة: أنها الإيثار، ألا ترى أن امرأة العزيز

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r6.speaker: أبو طلحة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r6.claim: The highest self-sacrifice is protecting the Messenger: at Uhud Abu Talha shielded him, begged him not to expose himself, and was struck in his hand while guarding him.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#7/r6.anchor: ففي الصحيح: أن أبا طلحة ترس على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم أحد

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r1.speaker: حذيفة العدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r1.claim: At Yarmuk, Huthayfa al-ʿAdawi successively offered water to his dying cousin, Hisham ibn al-ʿAs, and another wounded man; each directed the water to the next, and all three died.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r1.anchor: وقال حذيفة العدوي: انطلقت يوم اليرموك أطلب ابن عم لي ومعي شيء من الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r2.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r2.claim: A young man from Balkh told Abu Yazid that true asceticism is gratitude when one has something and preferring others when one has enough; he contrasted this with merely eating when able and enduring hunger otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r2.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد البسطامي: ما غلبني أحد ما غلبني شاب من أهل بلخ

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r3.speaker: ذو النون المصري
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r3.claim: Dhu al-Nun defined the open-hearted ascetic by three traits: distributing accumulated wealth, not seeking what is absent, and preferring others when food is scarce.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r3.anchor: وسئل ذو النون المصري: ما حد الزاهد المنشرح صدره

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الأنطاكي
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r4.claim: At a gathering of more than thirty men with too few loaves, they broke the bread, extinguished the lamp, and each left it for the others; afterward none had eaten.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r4.anchor: وحكي عن أبي الحسن الأنطاكي: أنه اجتمع عنده نيف وثلاثون رجلا

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r5.claim: Khassasa is a need that disrupts one's condition; its root sense is isolation, so it describes being left alone in want.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r5.anchor: الخصاصة: الحاجة التي تختل بها الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses khassasa for scarcity in a line saying spring sustains the sick and enriches the poor when need arises.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r6.anchor: أما الربيع إذا تكون خصاصة عاش السقيم به وأثرى المقتر

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r7.claim: Qurtubi initially treats shuhh and bukhl as equivalent terms for miserliness, with forms including shih, shuh, and shuhaha.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r7.anchor: يقال: رجل شحيح بين الشح والشح والشحاحة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r8.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r8.claim: Some lexicographers distinguish shuhh from bukhl as the more intense condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r8.anchor: وجعل بعض أهل اللغة الشح أشد من البخل

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r9.claim: Al-Sihah records alternate conjugations of shuhh and its singular and plural forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r9.anchor: وشححت أيضا تشح وتشح. ورجل شحيح، وقوم شحاح وأشحة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r10.claim: The verse's shuhh includes withholding zakat and non-obligatory duties such as kinship ties and hospitality; spending on these protects one from it, whereas spending lavishly on oneself while neglecting them does not.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r10.anchor: والمراد بالآية: الشح بالزكاة وما ليس بفرض من صلة ذوي الأرحام

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r11.claim: Al-Aswad reports that Ibn Masʿud told a man afraid of his stinginess that Qurʾanic shuhh means unjustly consuming another's wealth, while the man's own condition was bukhl.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#8/r11.anchor: وروى الأسود عن ابن مسعود أن رجلا أتاه فقال له

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r1.claim: Qurtubi underscores Ibn Masʿud's distinction between Qurʾanic shuhh and bukhl.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r1.anchor: ففرق رضي الله عنه بين الشح والبخل

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r2.speaker: طاووس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r2.claim: Tawus says bukhl is withholding one's own property, while shuhh is coveting what other people own by lawful or unlawful means and never being satisfied.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r2.anchor: وقال طاوس: البخل أن يبخل الإنسان بما في يده، والشح أن يشح بما في أيدي الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines shuhh as withholding zakat and storing up unlawful wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r3.anchor: ابن جبير: الشح منع الزكاة وادخار الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r4.speaker: ابن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna defines shuhh as injustice.

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r5.speaker: الليث
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r5.claim: Al-Layth defines shuhh as abandoning obligations and violating prohibitions.

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls one who follows desire and does not accept faith shuhh.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r6.anchor: ابن عباس: من اتبع هواه ولم يقبل بالإيمان فذلك الشحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says God has protected a person from shuhh if it neither induces him to take what God forbade nor prevents him from giving what God commanded.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r7.anchor: ابن زيد: من لم يأخذ شيئا لشيء نهاه الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r8.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r8.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that one is free of shuhh by paying zakat, hosting guests, and giving during hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r8.anchor: وقال أنس: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r9.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r9.claim: Anas also reports the Prophet seeking refuge from the soul's greed, extravagance, and intrusive thoughts.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r9.anchor: وعنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r10.speaker: أبو الهياج الأسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r10.claim: Abu al-Hayyaj saw ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf asking only to be protected from his own greed; Ibn ʿAwf explained that this protection keeps one from theft, adultery, and similar sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r10.anchor: وقال أبو الهياج الأسدي: رأيت رجلا في الطواف يدعو: اللهم قني شح نفسي

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r11.claim: The Prophet warned that injustice brings darkness on Judgment Day and that greed destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and violations of sacred limits.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r11.anchor: اتقوا الظلم فإن الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة واتقوا الشح

QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r12.speaker: كسرى
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r12.claim: Chosroes said greed harms people more than poverty: a poor person is satisfied when food appears, while a greedy person is never satisfied.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:9#9/r12.anchor: وقال كسرى لأصحابه: أي شيء أضر بابن آدم؟ قالوا: الفقر

QASHANI:59:7-9/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:7-9/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:7-9/r9.claim: The home and faith signify the original abode of primordial nature and the first covenant, the locus of faith; the lower soul is exile.
QASHANI:59:7-9/r9.anchor: المقر الأصلي الذي هو الفطرة الأولى والعهد الأول

QASHANI:59:7-9/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:7-9/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:7-9/r10.claim: “Before them” means before the emigrants’ migration from the exile of the soul to this original home, which precedes their former dwellings; Qashani cites the saying, “Love of homeland is part of faith.”
QASHANI:59:7-9/r10.anchor: من قبل هجرة المهاجرين من دار الغربة التي هي النفس إليها

QASHANI:59:7-9/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:7-9/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:7-9/r11.claim: These residents retained primordial purity without the soul’s veil, unlike the first emigrants, who became clouded and later regained purity through spiritual wayfaring.
QASHANI:59:7-9/r11.anchor: فهم الذين لم يسقطوا عن الفطرة ولم يحتجبوا بحجاب النفس في النشأة وبقوا على صفائها بخلاف الأولين الذين تكدروا وتغيروا ثم رجعوا إلى الصفاء بالسير والسلوك

QASHANI:59:7-9/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:7-9/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:7-9/r12.claim: They love the emigrants because of shared purity, original affinity, true kinship, and recollection of the prior covenant through religious agreement and brotherhood.
QASHANI:59:7-9/r12.anchor: لوجود الجنسية في الصفاء وتحقق المناسبة الأصلية والقرابة الحقيقية بالوفاء وتذكر العهد السابق بالموافقة في الدين والإخاء

QASHANI:59:7-9/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:7-9/r13.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:7-9/r13.claim: They feel no envy over the emigrants’ allotments because their hearts are safe from the soul’s afflictions and greed, detached from worldly shares, and certain of their own apportionment.
QASHANI:59:7-9/r13.anchor: لسلامة قلوبهم عن آفات النفوس وطهارتها عن دواعي الحرص وتنزهها عن محبة الحظوظ وتيقنها بالاقسام

QASHANI:59:9/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:9/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:9/r1.claim: They prefer others through detachment, turning toward the holy presence, innate virtue, and deep love for true brothers and companions on the path.
QASHANI:59:9/r1.anchor: لتجردهم وتوجههم إلى جناب القدس وترفهم عن مواد الرجس وكون الفضيلة لهم أمرا ذاتيا باقتضاء الفطرة وفرط محبة الإخوان بالحقيقة والأعوان في الطريقة

QASHANI:59:9/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:9/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:9/r2.claim: Giving others precedence despite hardship reflects chivalry, perfect manliness, strong unity, restraint from ego’s share, and fear of returning to partial desires after tasting universal ones.
QASHANI:59:9/r2.anchor: فتقديمهم أصحابهم على أنفسهم لمكان الفتوة وكمال المروءة ولقوة التوحيد والاحتراز عن حظ النفس وخوف الرجوع إلى المطالب الجزئية بعد وجدان الذوق من المطالب الكلية

QASHANI:59:9/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:9/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:9/r3.claim: Greed is intrinsic to the lower soul, which inclines downward and loves particular gains; it ends only with the soul, and deliverance from its evils comes through God’s protection.
QASHANI:59:9/r3.anchor: والشح من غرائزها المعجونة في طينتها لملازمتها الجهة السفلية ومحبتها الحظوظ الجزئية فلا ينتفي منها إلا عند انتفائها ولكن المعصوم من تلك الآفات والشرور من عصمه الله

QASHANI:59:9/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:9/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:9/r4.claim: The successful attain the perfections of the heart.

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r1.claim: Al-dār means Medina, the abode of emigration, which the Anṣār settled before the Emigrants.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r1.anchor: والمراد من الدار المدينة وهي دار الهجرة تبوأها الأنصار قبل المهاجرين

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r2.claim: To answer the objection that faith cannot be settled, he supplies an omitted coordinated sense: they settled the city and sincerely embraced faith; a poetic line supports this ellipsis.

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r3.claim: A second answer treats faith as their home and homeland because they were firmly established and steadfast in it; Salman likewise called himself a son of Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r3.anchor: جعلوا الإيمان مستقرا ووطنا لهم لتمكنهم منه واستقامتهم عليه

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r4.claim: A third answer takes al-īmān as a name for Medina, where faith appeared and grew strong.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r4.anchor: أنه سمى المدينة بالإيمان ، لأن فيها ظهر الإيمان وقوي

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r5.claim: To answer the chronology objection, one reading reorders the phrase: the Anṣār settled the city before the Emigrants, and settled faith.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r5.anchor: أن الكلام على التقديم والتأخير ، والتقدير : والذين تبوءوا الدار من قبلهم والإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r6.claim: Another answer supplies an omitted annexed phrase: they settled the city and faith before their own migration.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r6.anchor: أنه على تقدير حذف المضاف والتقدير : تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبل هجرتهم

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the need in their hearts as envy, emotional heat, and anger at what the Emigrants received instead of them.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن : أي حسدا وحرارة وغيظا مما أوتي المهاجرون من دونهم

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r8.claim: The verse calls envy and anger a need by metonymy, since such feelings are inseparable from need and are named by their necessary correlate.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r8.anchor: وأطلق لفظ الحاجة على الحسد والغيظ والحرارة ، لأن هذه الأشياء لا تنفك عن الحاجة

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r9.claim: The verb means preferring someone with something; its object is omitted, with the sense that they preferred the Emigrants in wealth and homes over themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r9.anchor: يقال : آثره بكذا إذا خصه به ، ومفعول الإيثار محذوف

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet offered the Anṣār a choice: share homes and wealth with the Emigrants while the Anṣār received no booty, or keep their property and leave the booty to the Emigrants; they chose to share, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال للأنصار : ( إن شئتم قسمتم

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r11.claim: Their preference was altruism amid poverty and need, not a sign that they had no need of wealth themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r11.anchor: فبين أن هذا الإيثار ليس غنى عن المال ، ولكنه عن حاجة وخصاصة وهي الفقر

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r12.claim: Khaṣāṣah originally refers to an opening or hole in a sieve, door, cloud, or veil; each such gap is a khaṣāṣah.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r12.anchor: وأصلها من الخصاص وهي الفرج ، وكل خرق في منخل أو باب أو سحاب أو برقع فهي خصاص

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r13.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r13.claim: Commentators recount the Anṣār giving food to a guest and pretending not to eat until he was full, and say the verse was revealed about this hospitality.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r13.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أنواعا من إيثار الأنصار للضيف بالطعام وتعللهم عنه حتى يشبع الضيف

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī says the verse was actually revealed because the Anṣār preferred the Emigrants in the fayʾ; the hospitality stories still fall under the verse's general meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r14.anchor: والصحيح أنها نزلت بسبب إيثارهم المهاجرين بالفيء ، ثم لا يمتنع أن يدخل فيها سائر الإيثارات

RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r15.claim: The word shuhḥ is read with either ḍamma or kasra on its first consonant.
RAZI-FULL:v29p249#3/r15.anchor: الشح بالضم والكسر ، وقد قرىء بهما

RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r1.claim: Bukhl is the act of withholding, whereas shuhḥ is the inward disposition that prompts withholding; shuhḥ is therefore an attribute of the soul.
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الفرق بين الشح والبخل هو أن البخل نفس المنع ،

RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r2.claim: Those protected from the soul's avarice are the successful, attaining what they seek.

RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says one is protected from shuhḥ by avoiding what God forbids taking and giving what God commands one to give.
RAZI-FULL:v29p250/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد : من لم يأخذ شيئا نهاه الله عن أخذه

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r1.claim: The land is Madinah; those settled there in belief are its Muslims who accepted Islam before the Prophet and the Emigrants arrived.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r1.anchor: In the land refers to Madinah, and those who were settled . . . in belief before them refers to the Muslims of Madinah

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r2.speaker: IK, W
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r2.claim: A report says an Ansari host and his wife fed a poor man from the People of the Veranda by giving him the children's food; the Prophet praised the couple, and the verse was revealed.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r2.anchor: The Prophet said, “Truly the dwellers of the heavens are amazed at what you two have done.” This verse was then revealed (IK, W).

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r3.claim: Preferring others is connected to verses praising the giving of wealth despite loving it.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r3.anchor: They prefer others over themselves is related to those verses that praise giving wealth despite loving it

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r4.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r4.claim: Aj reads the absence of need more broadly as removing worldly attachment from the heart, so one is not attached to what passes one by.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r4.anchor: removing this world from one’s heart, so that the heart is no longer attached to what passes it by (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r5.claim: A hadith says that renouncing the world wins God's love, while renouncing what belongs to others wins people's love.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r5.anchor: a ḥadīth states, “Abstain from the world, and God will love you; abstain

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r6.claim: Those protected from avarice feel no need for what is destined for others.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r6.anchor: thus describes those who feel no need for what is destined for others and are thereby protected

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r7.claim: A hadith calls the soul between one's sides one's worst enemy.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r7.anchor: anotherḥadīth, “Your worst enemy is the soul between your two sides.”

STUDYQURAN:59:9/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r8.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r8.claim: The Prophet warns against oppression, a darkness on Judgment Day, and avarice, which destroyed earlier peoples and led them to shed blood and legalize the unlawful.
STUDYQURAN:59:9/r8.anchor: the Prophet warned his followers, “Be on your guard against committing oppression, for oppression is a darkness on the Day of Resurrection.

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r6.claim: The verse concerns the Anṣār, who settled in Medina before the emigrants came from Mecca.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r6.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الأنصار . { تبوءو الدار } أي سكنوا المدينة قبل المهاجرين

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r7.claim: The Anṣār neither resented the emigrants' share of the booty nor inwardly objected to God's choice of them, even when they themselves were in need.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r7.anchor: ولا يحسدونهم على ذلك ، ولا يعترضون بقلوبهم على حكم الله بتخصيص المهاجرين ، حتى لو كانت بهم حاجة أو اختلال أحوال

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r8.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r8.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about an Anṣārī who received a sheep's head and passed it among seven households until it returned to the first.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r8.anchor: قيل نزلت الآية في رجل منهم أهديت له رأس شاة فطاف على سبعة أبيات حتى انتهى إلى الأول

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r9.speaker: وقيل
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r9.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about a man who served food to his guest and extinguished the lamp to make the guest think he was eating, preferring him and his family over himself.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r9.anchor: وقيل نزلت في رجل منهم نزل به ضيف فقرب منه الطعام وأطفأ السراج ليوهم ضيفه أنه يأكل

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r10.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r10.claim: A saying calls the generous person one who builds a house for guests and brethren, and the miser one who builds for himself.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r10.anchor: ويقال : الكريم من بنى الدار لضيفانه وإخوانه ( واللئيم من بناها لنفسه )

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r11.claim: The wording says whoever is protected from the self's stinginess, not merely whoever avoids stinginess.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r11.anchor: وقيل : لم يقل الله : ومن يتق شح نفسه بل قال : { ومن يوق شح نفسه }

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r12.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r12.claim: One saying describes altruism as giving preference to a person who is already full while oneself remains hungry.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r12.anchor: ويقال : صاحب الإيثار يؤثر الشبعان على نفسه - وهو جائع

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r13.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r13.claim: Another saying denies true altruism to anyone who distinguishes between people; the altruist prefers everyone without distinction.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r13.anchor: ويقال : من ميز بين شخص وشخص فليس بصاحب إيثار حتى يؤثر الجميع دون تمييز

QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r14.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r14.claim: Altruism sees what others hold as theirs and what comes into one's own hand as a trust awaiting permission to use.
QUSHAYRI:v3p304/r14.anchor: ويقال : الإيثار أن ترى أن ما بأيدي الناس لهم ، وأن ما يحصل في يدك ليس إلا كالوديعة والأمانة عندك

TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r1.claim: The Ansar settled in Medina, believed before the emigrants, and loved those who migrated to them.
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم} قال: الأنصار نعت

TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the described group as the Ansar.
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم} قال: الأنصار نعت

TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the Ansar welcomed their emigrant brethren into their homes and built mosques before the Prophet arrived; God praised them and affirmed the two groups' share in the fayʾ.
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون

TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says these are the Ansar, who loved the emigrants who came to them.
TAB-FULL:v22p524#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله عز وجل: {والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون}

TAB-FULL:v22p526/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r1.claim: The Ansar felt no envy over the fayʾ given to the emigrants when the Prophet allocated the Banu Nadir property to the early emigrants, except for two poor Ansar.
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا} [الحشر: 9] قال: الحسد

TAB-FULL:v22p526/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي بكر
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r2.claim: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr reports that Banu Nadir surrendered their property to the Prophet, who reserved it for himself to distribute as he wished and gave it to the early emigrants, apart from Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujana, who pleaded poverty.
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر، أنه حدث أن بني النضير خلوا الأموال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v22p526/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says some Ansar spoke about the Banu Nadir property, so God reproached them by recalling that they had not fought to win it; the Prophet offered shared harvest and service instead of dividing property, and they agreed.
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا} [الحشر: 9] المهاجرون، قال: وتكلم في ذلك

TAB-FULL:v22p526/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r4.claim: Al-Hasan explains the need or desire in their hearts as envy.
TAB-FULL:v22p526/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا} [الحشر: 9] قال: الحسد

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r1.claim: The Ansar gave their wealth to the emigrants ahead of themselves even when they themselves faced need and poverty.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليضيفه، فلم يكن عنده ما يضيفه

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r2.claim: Khasasah is a verbal noun and also a noun for need or a gap; it can describe openings in a wall, with plurals khasasat and khasas.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r2.anchor: والخصاصة مصدر، وهي أيضا اسم، وهو كل ما تخللته ببصرك كالكوة والفرجة في الحائط، تجمع خصاصات وخصاص

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r3.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r3.claim: An anonymous rajaz poet uses khasas for openings in a wall, supporting the lexical sense of gaps.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r3.anchor: كما قال الراجز: قد علم المقاتلات هجا والناظرات من خصاص لمجا

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when a guest came to the Prophet and he had no food to offer, Abu Talha hosted him; his wife put the children to sleep, extinguished the lamp, and let the guest eat, and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليضيفه، فلم يكن عنده ما يضيفه

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r5.claim: Another report from Abu Hurayra says an Ansari with only enough food for his family put the children to sleep, darkened the room, and served the guest; the verse about protection from shuhh was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رجلا من الأنصار بات به ضيف، فلم يكن عنده إلا قوته وقوت صبيانه

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r6.claim: Those whom God protects from their own shuhh are the successful, who remain in Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r6.anchor: من وقاه الله شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون المخلدون في الجنة

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r7.claim: In Arab usage, shuhh means stinginess and withholding surplus wealth; ʿAmr ibn Kulthum's description of a miser illustrates the sense.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r7.anchor: والشح في كلام العرب: البخل، ومنع الفضل من المال

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r8.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r8.claim: ʿAmr ibn Kulthum's poem uses al-shahih for a miser, supporting the meaning of stinginess.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r8.anchor: قول عمرو بن كلثوم: [البحر الوافر] ترى اللحز الشحيح

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r9.speaker: العلماء
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r9.claim: The scholars explain shuhh here as consuming other people's property without right.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r9.anchor: وأما العلماء فإنهم يرون أن الشح في هذا الموضع إنما هو: أكل أموال الناس بغير حق

TAB-FULL:v22p528/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r10.claim: Ibn Masud reassures a man worried about his own tightfistedness: the Quranic shuhh is wrongfully eating a brother's property, whereas ordinary withholding is bukhl.
TAB-FULL:v22p528/r10.anchor: عن أشعث بن أبي الشعثاء، عن أبيه، قال: أتى رجل ابن مسعود فقال: إني أخاف أن أكون قد هلكت

TAB-FULL:v22p531/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r1.claim: Ibn Masud tells a questioner that shuhh is taking a brother's wealth unjustly; merely keeping one's own money is bukhl.
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r1.anchor: جاء رجل إلى عبد الله بن مسعود، فقال: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، إني أخشى أن تكون أصابتني هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v22p531/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r2.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf repeatedly prayed for protection from shuhh, explaining that such protection keeps one from theft, adultery, and other sins.
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r2.anchor: فرأيت رجلا يقول: اللهم قني شح نفسي. لا يزيد على ذلك

TAB-FULL:v22p531/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r3.claim: The Prophet says one is free of shuhh by paying zakat, hosting a guest, and giving when calamity strikes.
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r3.anchor: قال: «برئ من الشح من أدى الزكاة، وقرى الضيف، وأعطى في النائبة»

TAB-FULL:v22p531/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says he feared miserliness over money he spent then wanted back; Abdullah ibn Safwan also judged him unprotected from shuhh because he approved of Uthman's killing.
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر، قال: إن نجوت من ثلاث طمعت أن أنجو

TAB-FULL:v22p531/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says protection from shuhh means taking nothing forbidden and not letting greed prevent one from withholding or giving as God directs.
TAB-FULL:v22p531/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله عز وجل: {ومن يوق شح نفسه} [الحشر: 9] قال: من وقي شح نفسه

TAB-FULL:v22p532/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p532/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p532/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says one is protected from self's shuhh by avoiding what God forbids and not withholding what He commands; such a person succeeds.
TAB-FULL:v22p532/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ومن يوق شح نفسه} [الحشر: 9] قال: من لم يأخذ شيئا لشيء نهاه الله

SULAMI:v2p318/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r1.speaker: أبو الحسين البوشيخي
SULAMI:v2p318/r1.claim: Abu al-Husayn al-Bushaykhi defines chivalry through the Ansar's welcome and selflessness, and through the Prophetic teaching that a believer wants for a brother what he wants for himself.
SULAMI:v2p318/r1.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن أحمد يقول : سئل أبو الحسين البوشيخي عن الفتوة ؟ فقال : الفتوة عندي ما وصف الله تعالى به الأنصار

SULAMI:v2p318/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v2p318/r2.claim: The Prophet defines faith through wanting for one's brother what one wants for oneself.
SULAMI:v2p318/r2.anchor: وفي قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' المؤمن الذي يرضى لأخيه ما يرضى لنفسه ' .

SULAMI:v2p318/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r3.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p318/r3.claim: Al-Qasim says a house devoted to chivalry and its people is praiseworthy, while one built for self-interest and display is blameworthy.
SULAMI:v2p318/r3.anchor: قال القاسم : من عمر داره للفتوة والفتيان كان محمودا ومن عمرها لنفسه والتزين به كان مذموما

SULAMI:v2p318/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p318/r4.claim: Ibn Ata says they prefer others with generosity even when they themselves are hungry.
SULAMI:v2p318/r4.anchor: قال أبن عطاء : يؤثرون به جودا وكرما ولو كان بهم خصاصة يعني جوعا .

SULAMI:v2p318/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r5.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v2p318/r5.claim: Abu Hafs defines altruism as placing the interests of one's companions before one's own in both worldly and religious matters.
SULAMI:v2p318/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حفص : الإيثار هو أن تقدم حظوظ الاخوان على حظك في أمر دنياك وآخرتك .

SULAMI:v2p318/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p318/r6.claim: Some say altruism is not a choice but putting every person's rights before one's own without distinction among people one knows.
SULAMI:v2p318/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الإيثار لا يكون عن اختيار إنما الإيثار أن تقدم حقوق الخلق اجمع على حقك ولا تميز في ذلك بين أخ وصاحب

SULAMI:v2p318/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r7.speaker: يوسف بن الحسين
SULAMI:v2p318/r7.claim: Yusuf ibn al-Husayn says true altruism belongs to one who sees all things as God's: whatever reaches them belongs more rightfully to God, and their hand is only a trustee's or a thief's hand returning it to its owner.
SULAMI:v2p318/r7.anchor: وقال يوسف بن الحسين : إنما الإيثار من رأى لنفسه ملكا لا يصح له الإيثار لأنه يرى نفسه أحق بالشيء

SULAMI:v2p318/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p318/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p318/r8.claim: Some say altruism means preferring one's brothers in their share of the afterlife; worldly life is too insignificant to merit such mention.
SULAMI:v2p318/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم : الإيثار أن تؤثر بحظ آخرتك على إخوانك فإن الدنيا أقل خطرا من أن يكون لإيثارها محل أو ذكر .

SULAMI:v2p319#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r1.claim: Sahl says those freed from the self's greed for anything besides God and His remembrance are successful and live on with God through His life.
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r1.anchor: قال سهل : حرص نفسه على شيء هو غير الله والذكر له فأولئك هم المفلحون الباقون مع الله أحياء بحياته .

SULAMI:v2p319#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says even one embodying Moses' sincerity, Abraham's courtesy, and the Beloved's character remains deprived if the innermost self gives anything importance or sees an interest of its own.
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r2.anchor: سئل الواسطي : متى ينجو العبد من شح نفسه ؟ قال : لو أتى بإخلاص الكليم وأدب الخليل وخلق الحبيب

SULAMI:v2p319#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r3.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says every miser wrongs another and seeks what is not rightfully theirs.
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل : ما شح أحد إلا ظلم غيره وطلب ما ليس له .

SULAMI:v2p319#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r4.claim: Some define miserliness as following one's nature and altruism as opposing the self.
SULAMI:v2p319#5/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الشح متابعة الطبع والإيثار مخالفة النفس .

TUSTARI:59:9/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:59:9/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:59:9/r1.claim: Khaṣāṣa means hunger and poverty; Arabs call an impoverished person makhṣūṣ.
TUSTARI:59:9/r1.anchor: تقول العرب: فلان مخصوص إذا كان فقيرا

TUSTARI:59:9/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:59:9/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:59:9/r2.claim: The people of Medina prefer God's pleasure to their own desire, and their selflessness is evidence of love.
TUSTARI:59:9/r2.anchor: فيؤثرون رضا الله على هواهم، والإيثار شاهد الحب

TUSTARI:59:9/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:59:9/r3.speaker: وهيب بن الورد
TUSTARI:59:9/r3.claim: Wahib ibn al-Ward transmits God's oath: one who prefers God's desire has worries reduced, affairs gathered, heart freed of poverty, and wealth before the eyes; one who prefers self accumulates worries, loses order and inner wealth, and is left to perish.
TUSTARI:59:9/r3.anchor: وقد حكي عن وهيب بن الورد أنه قال: يقول الله تعالى

TUSTARI:59:9/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:59:9/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:59:9/r4.claim: Being spared the soul's avarice means not clinging to anything besides God and His remembrance; such people abide with God in a good life.
TUSTARI:59:9/r4.anchor: أي ومن يوق حرص نفسه وبخلها على شيء هو غير الله وغير ذكره

TABATABAI:59:8-9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r8.claim: One view treats the verse as a fresh sentence praising the Anṣār and consoling them for not receiving the fayʾ; the relative clause is subject and their love of emigrants is its predicate.
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r8.anchor: قيل إنه استئناف مسوق لمدح الأنصار لتطيب بذلك قلوبهم إذ لم يشركوا في الفيء

TABATABAI:59:8-9/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r9.claim: Settling in the abode is a figurative way to describe building a religious community where believers can take refuge.
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r9.anchor: والمراد بتبوي الدار وهو تعميرها بناء مجتمع ديني يأوي إليه المؤمنون

TABATABAI:59:8-9/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r10.claim: Settling faith means cultivating it in practice and removing impediments, so its acts of obedience and devotion can be performed freely, as they could not in Mecca.
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r10.anchor: وتبوي الإيمان وتعميره رفع نواقصه من حيث العمل بحيث يستطاع العمل بما يدعو إليه

TABATABAI:59:8-9/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r11.claim: Another possible parsing coordinates faith with the verb they settled, supplying an omitted governing verb meaning they preferred faith.
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r11.anchor: على تبوؤا وقد حذف الفعل العامل فيه

TABATABAI:59:8-9/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r12.claim: Another view coordinates the Anṣār with the emigrants, making the Anṣār participants in the fayʾ.
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا يشارك الأنصار المهاجرين في الفيء

TABATABAI:59:8-9/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r13.claim: The report that the Prophet gave some fayʾ to three poor Anṣār supports their participation: if they could receive none, not even three could have received it; the Prophet chose the allocation pattern.
TABATABAI:59:8-9/r13.anchor: فإعطاء بعضهم منه دليل على مشاركتهم لهم غير أن الأمر لما كان راجعا إلى النبي

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r1.claim: Given that poor emigrants exemplify spending in God’s cause, the Anṣār and later generations are best read as coordinated with the emigrants, not as fresh independent clauses.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r1.anchor: بل ما ورد من إعطائه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للثلاثة يؤيد هذا الوجه بعينه

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r2.claim: The report that the Prophet gave fayʾ to three Anṣār supports their inclusion; if only poor emigrants had a share, no Anṣār should have received any, while many Anṣār were poor and in need.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r2.anchor: بل ما ورد من إعطائه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للثلاثة يؤيد هذا الوجه بعينه

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to the emigrants, and means the Anṣār settled there before the emigrants arrived in Medina.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r3.anchor: للمهاجرين والمراد من قبل مجيئهم وهجرتهم إلى المدينة

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r4.claim: The Anṣār love those who migrated to them because they left the abode of disbelief for the abode of faith and the Muslim community.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r4.anchor: أي يحبون من هاجر إليهم لأجل هجرتهم من دار الكفر إلى دار الإيمان

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r5.claim: The pronouns in they find and their hearts refer to the Anṣār, while the pronoun in they were given refers to the emigrants; min is partitive.

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r6.claim: The Anṣār feel no desire for the emigrants’ allotment and are not resentful or envious of the fayʾ being distributed to them.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r6.anchor: فلا يضيق نفوسهم من تقسيم الفيء بين المهاجرين دونهم ولا يحسدون

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r7.claim: Another view understands ḥājah as the anger or resentment that need can produce.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد بالحاجة ما يؤدي إليه الحاجة وهو الغيظ

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r8.claim: Īthār means choosing and giving precedence to something over another.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r8.anchor: إيثار الشيء اختياره وتقديمه على غيره، والخصاصة الفقر والحاجة

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r9.claim: They put the emigrants ahead of themselves even while poor and in need.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r9.anchor: والمعنى ويقدمون المهاجرين على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم فقر وحاجة

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r10.claim: This is stronger praise than the preceding trait: they not only refrain from wanting the emigrants’ possessions but give them their own despite need.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r10.anchor: وهذه الخصيصة أغزر وأبلغ في مدحهم من الخصيصة السابقة فالكلام في معنى الإضراب

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r11.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r11.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that a gap in a house is called khaṣāṣ and by extension poverty is a deficiency left unfilled, like khallah.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r11.anchor: قال الراغب خصاص البيت فرجه وعبر عن الفقر الذي لم يسد بالخصاصة

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r12.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r12.claim: Al-Rāghib defines shuh as miserliness coupled with acquisitiveness in what is customary.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r12.anchor: قال الراغب الشح بخل مع حرص فيما كان عادة انتهى

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r13.claim: Yūq is a passive imperfect of protection: whoever God protects from inner constriction about giving or distress at others’ possessions succeeds.
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r13.anchor: فعل مضارع مجهول من الوقاية بمعنى الحفظ

TABATABAI:59:8-10/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:8-10/r14.claim: Those whom God protects from the constriction of their souls are the successful.

TABATABAI:59:1-10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r8.claim: A report from Imam al-Ṣādiq says faith is a house, as are Islam and disbelief.
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r8.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث الإيمان بعضه من بعض وهو دار وكذلك الإسلام دار

TABATABAI:59:1-10/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports Imam al-Bāqir’s statement that religion is love, citing verses about loving God, faith being beloved, and the Anṣār loving emigrants; he concludes religion and love are one.
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r9.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة عن أبي جعفرعليه السلام في حديث قال يا زياد ويحك وهل الدين إلا الحب

TABATABAI:59:1-10/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r10.claim: An unattributed hadith cited in al-Majmaʿ says miserliness cannot coexist with faith in a Muslim’s heart, nor dust from God’s cause with Hell’s smoke inside him.
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r10.anchor: وفي المجمع وفي الحديث لا يجتمع الشح والإيمان في قلب رجل مسلم

TABATABAI:59:1-10/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r11.claim: Al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurrah reports Imam al-Ṣādiq’s view that shuh is worse than miserliness: it covets both one’s own and others’ property, even by unlawful means, and is never content with God’s provision.
TABATABAI:59:1-10/r11.anchor: قال لي أبو عبد الله عليه السلام أتدري من الشحيح

AKHFASH:v2p538#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p538#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p538#2/r5.claim: He glosses مما أوتوا as مما أعطوا, what they gave.
AKHFASH:v2p538#2/r5.anchor: وقال {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة [175 ب] مما أوتوا} أي: مما أعطوا

TABRISI:59:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9/r1.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:59:9/r1.claim: On the day of Banu Nadir, the Prophet offered the Ansar a choice: share homes and property with the emigrants and share the booty, or keep their property and receive none of it.
TABRISI:59:9/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم بني النضير للأنصار

TABRISI:59:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9/r2.speaker: الأنصار
TABRISI:59:9/r2.claim: The Ansar chose to share their wealth and homes and give the emigrants all the booty without taking a share themselves; the verse was revealed about this.
TABRISI:59:9/r2.anchor: فقال الأنصار: بل نقسم لهم من أموالنا وديارنا ونؤثرهم بالغنيمة ولا نشاركهم فيها فنزلت

TABRISI:59:9/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:59:9/r3.claim: One reported occasion is seven thirsty men at Uhud who passed a cup of water along; all died without drinking, and God praised them.
TABRISI:59:9/r3.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في سبعة عطشوا في يوم أحد فجيء بماء يكفي لأحدهم فقال واحد منهم ناول فلانا

TABRISI:59:9/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:59:9/r4.claim: Another occasion is an Ansari who hosted a hungry visitor of the Prophet, serving the children's food while the couple pretended to eat and went to bed hungry; the Prophet recited this verse in the morning.
TABRISI:59:9/r4.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في رجل جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أطعمني فإني جائع فبعث إلى أهله

TABRISI:59:9/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TABRISI:59:9/r5.claim: In the account with a sound chain from Abu Hurayra, the host who hid the lack of food and put out the lamp was Ali and Fatima.
TABRISI:59:9/r5.anchor: وأما الذي رويناه بإسناد صحيح عن أبي هريرة أن الذي أضافه ونوم الصبية وأطفأ السراج علي ع وفاطمة ع

TABRISI:59:9-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r1.claim: The Ansar settled in Medina, the abode of the Hijra, before the emigrants; the wording's estimate is that they settled the abode and embraced faith before them.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r1.anchor: يعني المدينة وهي دار الهجرة تبوأها الأنصار قبل المهاجرين وتقدير الآية والذين تبوؤوا الدار من قبلهم

TABRISI:59:9-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r2.claim: Faith is coordinated with abode in wording, not sense, because faith is not a place one can settle; the intended sense is that they chose faith.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r2.anchor: وعطف الإيمان على الدار في الظاهر لا في المعنى لأن الإيمان ليس بمكان يتبوؤوأ لتقدير وآثروا الإيمان

TABRISI:59:9-10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:59:9-10/r3.claim: One interpretation takes before them to mean before the emigrants arrived in Medina.

TABRISI:59:9-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:59:9-10/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes it as before the emigrants believed and identifies the group as the seventy men at Aqaba who pledged to fight all peoples.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r4.anchor: وقيل: معناه قبل إيمان المهاجرين والمراد به أصحاب ليلة العقبة وهم سبعون رجلا بايعوا رسول الله

TABRISI:59:9-10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r5.claim: The Ansar loved the emigrants because they welcomed them into their homes and shared their property with them.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r5.anchor: لأنهم أحسنوا إلى المهاجرين وأسكنوهم دورهم وأشركوهم في أموالهم

TABRISI:59:9-10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r6.claim: They felt no envy, resentment, or anger about the Banu Nadir wealth given to the emigrants instead of to them.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r6.anchor: أي لا يجدون في قلوبهم حسدا وحزازة وغيظا مما أعطي المهاجرون دونهم من مال بني النضير

TABRISI:59:9-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r7.claim: They preferred the emigrants, putting them ahead of themselves in their wealth and homes, even though they themselves were in need; this makes their reward greater.

TABRISI:59:9-10/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:59:9-10/r8.claim: Anas ibn Malik reportedly swore that there were no misers among the Ansar and recited this verse.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r8.anchor: ويروى أن أنس بن مالك كان يحلف بالله تعالى ما في الأنصار بخيل ويقرأ هذه الآية

TABRISI:59:9-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r9.claim: To be protected from the soul's avarice is to be kept from its miserliness; such people succeed and win God's reward and Paradise.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r9.anchor: ومن يدفع عنه ويمنع عنه بخل نفسه

TABRISI:59:9-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:59:9-10/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says one is spared avarice by not taking what God forbids and not withholding what God commands one to give.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r10.anchor: وقيل: من لم يأخذ شيئا نهاه الله عنه

TABRISI:59:9-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:59:9-10/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies avarice as taking unlawful wealth and withholding alms.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r11.anchor: وقيل: شح النفس هو أخذ الحرام ومنع الزكاة عن سعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:59:9-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r12.speaker: الحديث
TABRISI:59:9-10/r12.claim: A hadith says avarice does not coexist with faith in a Muslim's heart, nor dust from God's path with Hell's smoke in his body.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r12.anchor: لا يجتمع الشح والإيمان في قلب رجل مسلم ولا يجتمع غبار في سبيل الله ودخان جهنم

TABRISI:59:9-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r13.claim: One parsing makes the Ansar an initial subject whose predicate is that they love the emigrants; the Prophet gave them little of the Fay, with reports differing between two and three men.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r13.anchor: أحدهما: أنه رفع على الابتداء وخبره يحبون من هاجر إليهم إلى آخره لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يقسم لهم شيئا

TABRISI:59:9-10/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:9-10/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:9-10/r14.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is genitive, coordinated with the poor emigrants, and the following description of the Ansar is a circumstantial clause.
TABRISI:59:9-10/r14.anchor: والآخر: أنه في موضع جر عطفا على الفقراء المهاجرين وعلى هذا فيكون قوله يحبون من هاجر إليهم

THALABI:v9p277#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p277#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p277#2/r4.claim: Those who settled the abode are the Ansar, who made Medina the home of faith and migration.
THALABI:v9p277#2/r4.anchor: والذين تبوؤا: توطنوا الدار اي اتخذوا المدينة دار الإيمان والهجرة، وهم الأنصار

THALABI:v9p277#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p277#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p277#2/r5.claim: The Ansar embraced Islam where they lived and built mosques two years before the Prophet arrived in Medina.
THALABI:v9p277#2/r5.anchor: وهم الأنصار أسلموا في ديارهم وبنوا المساجد قبل قدوم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسنتين

THALABI:v9p277#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p277#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p277#2/r6.claim: The verse means the Ansar settled Medina before the Muhajirun came to them.
THALABI:v9p277#2/r6.anchor: ونظم الآية: والذين تبوءوا الدار من قبلهم أي من قبل قدوم المهاجرين عليهم

THALABI:v9p277#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p277#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p277#2/r7.claim: حاجة here means resentment, vexation, or envy about the fay given to the migrants; after Banu Nadir, the Prophet gave them its property while leaving the Ansar aside except for three.
THALABI:v9p277#2/r7.anchor: ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة حزازة وغيظا وحسدا مما أوتوا أي مما أعطوا المهاجرين من الفيء

THALABI:v9p278/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p278/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p278/r1.claim: The Ansar preferred their migrant brothers in property and homes despite their own need and poverty.
THALABI:v9p278/r1.anchor: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم إخوانهم من المهاجرين بأموالهم وديارهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة: فاقة وحاجة

THALABI:v9p278/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p278/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v9p278/r2.claim: A hungry visitor asked the Prophet for food; an Ansari hosted him, hid that the family had only the children's food, and staged eating by lamplight so the guest could eat his fill. The hosts went to bed hungry, and the Prophet said God admired them.
THALABI:v9p278/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد أصابه الجهد فقال: يا رسول الله، إني جائع فأطعمني.

THALABI:v9p279/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p279/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v9p279/r1.claim: Anas says a roasted sheep's head passed successively among nine needy Companions, each giving it to another, until it returned to the first; the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v9p279/r1.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: أهدي لبعض الصحابة رأس شاة مشوي وكان مجهودا، فوجهه إلى جار له

THALABI:v9p279/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p279/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن الأنطاكي
THALABI:v9p279/r2.claim: A group of more than thirty men near Rayy put out the lamp and sat before a few loaves; afterward all the bread remained untouched because each preferred the others.
THALABI:v9p279/r2.anchor: ويحكى عن أبي الحسن الأنطاكي أنه اجتمع عنده نيف وثلاثون رجلا بقرية بقرب الري

THALABI:v9p279/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p279/r3.speaker: حذيفة العدوي
THALABI:v9p279/r3.claim: At Yarmuk, Huthayfa carried water to his wounded cousin, who directed it to Hisham ibn al-As; Hisham then directed it to another man. All three died before drinking.
THALABI:v9p279/r3.anchor: ويحكى عن حذيفة العدوي قال: انطلقت يوم اليرموك لطلب ابن عم لي ومعي شيء من ماء

THALABI:v9p279/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p279/r4.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
THALABI:v9p279/r4.claim: A young pilgrim from Balkh rebuked Abu Yazid's definition of asceticism as eating when food is found and enduring when it is absent; the youth said true ascetics endure scarcity and give others food when they have it.
THALABI:v9p279/r4.anchor: عن أبي يزيد البسطامي قال: ما غلبني أحد مثل ما غلبني شاب من أهل بلخ قدم علينا حاجا

THALABI:v9p279/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p279/r5.speaker: ذو النون المصري
THALABI:v9p279/r5.claim: Dhu al-Nun names three marks of an open-hearted ascetic: giving away accumulated goods, ceasing to seek what is lost, and preferring others when provisions are scarce.
THALABI:v9p279/r5.anchor: سئل ذو النون المصري عن علامة الزاهد المشروح صدره فقال: ثلاث: تفريق المجموع، وترك طلب المفقود

THALABI:v9p279/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p279/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p279/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that on the day of Banu Nadir the Prophet offered the Ansar a choice: share their homes and wealth with the migrants and receive a share of the spoils, or keep their property without a spoils share.
THALABI:v9p279/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) يوم النضير للأنصار: «إن شئتم قسمتم للمهاجرين من أموالكم ودياركم

THALABI:v9p280/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r1.speaker: الأنصار
THALABI:v9p280/r1.claim: The Ansar chose to divide their homes and wealth with the migrants, giving them the distribution without taking a share of that campaign's spoils; God then revealed the verse.
THALABI:v9p280/r1.anchor: فقالت الأنصار: بل نقسم لهم من أموالنا وديارنا ونؤثرهم بالقسمة ولا نشاركهم فيها.

THALABI:v9p280/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p280/r2.claim: In Arabic, shuh means miserliness and withholding one's surplus; early scholars also distinguished it from bukhl.
THALABI:v9p280/r2.anchor: والشح في كلام العرب: البخل ومنع الفضل، يقال: فلان شحيح من الشح والشح والشحة والشحاحة،

THALABI:v9p280/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r3.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
THALABI:v9p280/r3.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's line uses شحيح to describe a miser who grudgingly parts with his money, illustrating the term's sense.
THALABI:v9p280/r3.anchor:
قال عمرو بن كلثوم:
ترى اللحز الشحيح إذا أمرت

THALABI:v9p280/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v9p280/r4.claim: Ibn Masud tells a man afraid of ruin for being stingy that Qur'anic shuh is consuming another's property unjustly; ordinary stinginess is bukhl, also blameworthy.
THALABI:v9p280/r4.anchor: عن أبي الشعثاء قال: قال رجل لعبد الله بن مسعود: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، إني أخاف أن أكون

THALABI:v9p280/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p280/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets protection from shuh as resisting one's own desire and accepting faith.
THALABI:v9p280/r5.anchor: الوالبي علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: ومن يوق شح نفسه قال: يقول: هوى نفسه يتبع هواه فلم يقبل الإيمان

THALABI:v9p280/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v9p280/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the protected person neither takes what God forbids nor withholds what God commands.
THALABI:v9p280/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: من لم يأخذ شيئا لشيء نهاه الله سبحانه ولم يدعه الشح

THALABI:v9p280/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r7.speaker: طاوس
THALABI:v9p280/r7.claim: Tawus distinguishes bukhl as withholding what one possesses from shuh as begrudging what belongs to other people.
THALABI:v9p280/r7.anchor: وقال طاوس: البخل أن يبخل الإنسان بما في يديه، والشح أن يبخل بما في أيدي الناس.

THALABI:v9p280/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p280/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v9p280/r8.claim: The Prophet says a person is free of shuh if he pays zakat, hosts guests, and gives in times of adversity.
THALABI:v9p280/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «برئ من الشح من أدى الزكاة، وقرى الضيف

THALABI:v9p282/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p282/r2.speaker: مالك بن أنس
THALABI:v9p282/r2.claim: Malik says anyone who disparages a Companion or harbors resentment toward them has no entitlement to the Muslims' fay, citing the passage from the distribution verses through the prayer for later believers.
THALABI:v9p282/r2.anchor: قال مالك بن أنس: من ينتقص أحدا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان في قلبه عليهم غل، فليس له حق في فيء المسلمين،

FARRA:v3p144/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p144/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p144/r6.claim: When the Muhajirun received the Banu Nadir fay, the Prophet offered the Ansar either to share homes and property while receiving a comparable fay share, or to keep their own property. They chose to share their property without sharing the fay.
FARRA:v3p144/r6.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه للأنصار: إن شئتم قسمتم لهم من دوركم وأموالكم، وقسمت لكم كما قسمت لهم، وإما أن يكون لهم القسم، ولكم دياركم وأموالكم،

FARRA:v3p144/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p144/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p144/r7.claim: These words praise the Ansar: those they love are the Muhajirun, and they did not resent the migrants receiving the fay share.
FARRA:v3p144/r7.anchor: فأنزل الله جل وعز هذه الآيات ثناء على الأنصار، فقال: «يحبون من هاجر إليهم» (9) يعنى المهاجرين: «ولا يجدون في صدورهم» (9) الآية.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r1.claim: The abode is Medina, the home of migration, which the Anṣār settled before the Emigrants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: ثم ذكر الأنصار وأثنى عليهم حين طابت أنفسهم عن الفيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r2.claim: Maqātil estimates the syntax as the Anṣār settling the abode before the Emigrants and adopting faith, since they did not believe before the Emigrants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r2.anchor: وتقدير الآية: والذين تبوؤا الدار من قبلهم والإيمان, لأن الأنصار لم يؤمنوا قبل المهاجرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r3.claim: Faith is coordinated with the abode although the verb governing the abode does not govern faith; the sense is that they preferred faith, as in Arabic examples joining unlike objects.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r3.anchor: وعطف الإيمان على الدار، ولا يحسن إعمال الفعل الذي نصب الدار في الإيمان، ولكن المعنى، وآثروا الإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r4.claim: The phrase can mean they settled the abode and adopted faith, or can treat settling faith as a metaphor; both constructions are possible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: ومعنى الآية: تبوأوا الدار واعتقدوا الإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī supports the metaphorical construction with the idiom of settling among a clan’s elite and a poetic use of being settled in one’s clan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تبوأوا الإيمان على طريق المثل كما تقول: تبوأ من بني فلان الصميم، وعلى ذلك قول الشاعر:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r1.claim: The Anṣār felt no envy, resentment, or anger over what the Emigrants received instead of them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r1.anchor: المفسرون: حسدا وحزازة وغيظا مما أوتي المهاجرون دونهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r2.claim: A ḥāja is anything a person finds in the breast that is burdensome and needs to be removed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r2.anchor: وكل ما يجده الإنسان في صدره مما يحتاج إلى إزالته وشق عليه وجوده فهو حاجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r3.claim: Āthartuka means to prefer someone; īthār is to single someone out and favor them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r3.anchor: يقال: آثرتك إيثارا، أي: فضلتك، وآثره بكذا إذا خصه به وفضله من بين الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r4.claim: The omitted object is them: the Anṣār preferred the Emigrants in wealth and homes, sharing their houses and possessions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r4.anchor: ومفعول الإيثار محذوف والتقدير: ويؤثرونهم على أنفسهم، قال المفسرون: أي بأموالهم ومنازلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet offered the Anṣār either a share in the Emigrants’ homes and wealth plus a share of the fayʾ, or the Emigrants’ share of fayʾ with the Anṣār keeping their property; they chose to share their property and leave the fayʾ to the Emigrants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي، عن ابن عباس: هو أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال للأنصار:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r6.claim: Khaṣāṣa means poverty or need, from gaps and openings called khaṣāṣ in a sieve, door, cloud, or veil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r6.anchor: فبين أن هذا الإيثار ليس عن غنى من المال، ولكنه عن حاجة وخصاصة، وهي الفقر، وذو الخصاصة ذو الخلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r7.speaker: الراجز
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r7.claim: The rajaz line uses khaṣāṣ for an opening through which eyes look, illustrating the word’s sense of a gap.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r8.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r8.claim: Exegetes also report the Anṣār giving food to a guest and enduring hunger until the guest was full, and say the verse was revealed for this act.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r8.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أنواعا من إيثار الأنصار للضيف بالطعام وتعللهم عه حتى شبع الضيف، ثم ذكروا أن الآية نزلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r9.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the sound occasion was the Anṣār’s preference for the Emigrants in the fayʾ; the verse may also include the other reported forms of generosity.
