WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p380#2/r9.anchor: والصحيح أن الآية نزلت بسبب إيثارهم المهاجرين بالفيء ثم يجوز أن يتضمن قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī refers back to his explanation of avarice in 4:128.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r1.anchor: ذكرنا تفسير الشح في قوله: {وأحضرت الأنفس الشح}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r2.claim: Avarice is taking what is unlawful and withholding zakat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: هو أخذ الحرام ومنع الزكاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r4.claim: One is protected from avarice by neither taking what God forbade nor withholding what God commanded one to pay.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: من لم يأخذ شيئا نهاه الله عنه ولم يمنع شيئا أمره الله بأدائه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r5.claim: The Anṣār were protected from avarice when they willingly yielded the fayʾ to the Emigrants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p382/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: يعني أن الأنصار ممن وقي شح نفسه حين طابت أنفسهم عن الفيء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r3.claim: Those who settled in the abode and faith before the emigrants are the Ansar, who came to Medina and accepted faith.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r3.anchor: والذين تبوؤا الدار والإيمان } نزلوا المدينة وقبلوا الإيمان { من قبلهم } من قبل المهاجرين وهم الأنصار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r4.claim: Those whom the Ansar love are their fellow Muslims who emigrated to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r4.anchor: يحبون من هاجر إليهم } من المسلمين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r5.claim: They feel no resentment or envy over the fay' given to the emigrants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r5.anchor: ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة } غيظا وحسدا { مما أوتوا } مما أوتي المهاجرون من الفيء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r6.claim: The Prophet distributed the wealth of Banu Nadir among the emigrants and gave it to only three needy Ansar; the other Ansar accepted this graciously.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r6.anchor: وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم أموال بني النضير بين المهاجرين، ولم يعط الأنصار منها شيئا إلا ثلاثة نفر، كانت بهم حاجة فطابت أنفس الأنصار بذلك، فذلك قوله:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r7.claim: The Ansar choose their emigrant brothers over themselves by giving them wealth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r7.anchor: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم } أي: يختارون إخوانهم المهاجرين بالمال على أنفسهم { ولو كانت بهم خصاصة } حاجة وفاقة إلى المال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r8.claim: Khasasah means need and lack of money.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r8.anchor: ولو كانت بهم خصاصة } حاجة وفاقة إلى المال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r9.claim: Shuh is destructive greed for wealth that leads one to withhold people's due rights and to envy.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r9.anchor: ومن يوق شح نفسه } من حفظ من الحرص المهلك على المال، وهو حرص يحمله على إمساك المال عن الحقوق والحسد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r10.claim: Those protected from the greed of their souls are the successful.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:59:8-9/r10.anchor: ومن يوق شح نفسه } من حفظ من الحرص المهلك على المال، وهو حرص يحمله على إمساك المال عن الحقوق والحسد { فأولئك هم المفلحون

ELMALILI:59:9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r1.claim: “Those who settled the abode and faith” refers to the Ansar.
ELMALILI:59:9/r1.anchor: Ve şunlar ki bunlardan murad ensardır.

ELMALILI:59:9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r2.claim: The author prefers connecting the Ansar to the Muhajirun; this gives them a share in fayʾ like the Muhajirun.
ELMALILI:59:9/r2.anchor: Birincisi “muhâcirîn” üzerine ma‘tuf olmasıdır ki en râcih olan da budur.

ELMALILI:59:9/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r3.claim: A second analysis connects them to فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ, making their participation in sincerity explicit and their share in fayʾ implicit.
ELMALILI:59:9/r3.anchor: Bu surette onlara sadakatte iştirakleri tasrih edilmiş, fey’e iştirak hakları delâleten anlatılmış olur.

ELMALILI:59:9/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r4.claim: A third analysis takes the waw as introductory, with الذين as subject and يحبون as predicate; their virtues are stated independently, while fayʾ entitlement remains implicit.
ELMALILI:59:9/r4.anchor: Üçüncüsü ma‘tuf olmayıp vav istînâfiye, وَٱلَّذِينَ mübtedâ, يُحِبُّونَ haber olmaktır.

ELMALILI:59:9/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r5.claim: In any syntactic analysis, praising altruism presupposes a right or entitlement to relinquish; preference has no sense where there is no right to give up.
ELMALILI:59:9/r5.anchor: Çünkü üç takdirde de îsâr ile medih, esas itibariyle bir istihkak veya salâhiyetin sübûtunu ifade eder.

ELMALILI:59:9/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r6.claim: Tabawwaʾ can mean preparing or being prepared, as well as taking a place or abode.
ELMALILI:59:9/r6.anchor: تبوئه وتبوء gibi hazırlamak ve hazırlanmak mânalarına geldiği gibi

ELMALILI:59:9/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r7.claim: The verb can also mean lodging in a place, marrying, or taking a place as one's abode.
ELMALILI:59:9/r7.anchor: bir mekâna, bir konağa konmak, tezevvüc etmek

ELMALILI:59:9/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r8.claim: Al-dār denotes a bounded, fully equipped dwelling or homeland; here it means the abode of Islam, indicated by the mention of faith.
ELMALILI:59:9/r8.anchor: Burada “ed-dâr”dan murad da iman karînesiyle dâr-ı İslâm’dır.

ELMALILI:59:9/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r9.claim: Exegetes identify the first abode of Islam as Medina, where Muslims first lived and Islamic civilization began to develop.
ELMALILI:59:9/r9.anchor: ilk dâr-ı İslâm, ehl-i İslâm’ın ilk barındığı ve İslâm medeniyetinin ilk inkişâfa başladığı Medîne-i Münevvere olduğundan müfessirîn bunu Medine diye tefsir etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:59:9/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r10.speaker: İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:59:9/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats al-īmān as a comitative object coordinated with al-dār; this avoids supplying an omitted verb such as “they sincerely embraced faith.”
ELMALILI:59:9/r10.anchor: İbn Atıyye’nin dediği gibi mef‘ûl-i ma‘ah olması da güzel bir vecihtir.

ELMALILI:59:9/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r11.claim: Although some Muhajirun believed earlier, the Ansar preceded them in preparing Medina as an abode through faith, so they are called the ones who came before.
ELMALILI:59:9/r11.anchor: iman ile Medine’yi ihzar etmek itibariyle ensar mukaddem olduğu cihetle مِن قَبْلِهِمْ buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:59:9/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r12.claim: Min qablihim may mean before the migrants' arrival; īmān may also derive from the causative of safety, describing the Ansar securing Medina as an Islamic abode by the Aqaba pledge.
ELMALILI:59:9/r12.anchor: burada مِن قَبْلِهِمْ onların hicretlerinden evvel demek olabileceği gibi; “îmân”, “emn” ü “emân”dan if‘âl olmak da melhuzdur.

ELMALILI:59:9/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r13.claim: On this reading, the Ansar secured Medina as an abode of Islam before the migration through the Aqaba pledge.
ELMALILI:59:9/r13.anchor: ensar, muhâcirînin hicretinden evvel Akabe Bey’atı’yla vatanları olan Medine’yi dâr-ı İslâm yapmak üzere te’mîn edip imana sâhip oldular.

ELMALILI:59:9/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r14.claim: The Ansar loved those who migrated to them, beginning with the Prophet, whether the migrants were rich or poor; this displayed their sincerity.
ELMALILI:59:9/r14.anchor: başta Peygamber olmak üzere hicret eden o sâdıkları gerek zengin

ELMALILI:59:9/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r15.claim: They felt no inward regret about what was given to the migrants from fayʾ or other resources, as though it had been something they themselves needed.
ELMALILI:59:9/r15.anchor: yani muhacirlere gerek fey’ ve gerek sâireden verilen

ELMALILI:59:9/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r16.claim: The object of īthār is omitted; it may be the migrants or, more broadly, fellow believers whose needs the Ansar put ahead of their own.
ELMALILI:59:9/r16.anchor: Burada “îsâr”ın mef‘ûlü hazfedilmiştir. Binâen‘aleyh muhâcirîn yahut da e‘am olmak muhtemildir.

ELMALILI:59:9/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9/r17.claim: They gave others' needs precedence over their own, even when they themselves lacked necessities; the author calls this the highest generosity and selflessness.
ELMALILI:59:9/r17.anchor: daha üstün tutarak onları nefislerine takdim ve tercih ederler

ELMALILI:59:9/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r18.speaker: Müfessirînin bir kısmı
ELMALILI:59:9/r18.claim: A report about the distribution of Banu Nadir property says the Prophet allocated it to the Muhajirun, apart from three needy Ansar; the Ansar then offered their own wealth and homes and declined a share in that booty. Some exegetes call this the occasion of revelation.
ELMALILI:59:9/r18.anchor: Müfessirînin bir kısmı sebeb-i nüzûlün bu olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:59:9/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9/r19.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:59:9/r19.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that an Ansari, identified as Abu Talha in one version, hosted a starving man; the couple put their child to sleep, extinguished the lamp, and went hungry, after which the Prophet said God was pleased with them and the verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:59:9/r19.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim, Tirmizî, Nesâî ve daha bazıları Ebû Hüreyre’den şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r1.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that a sheep's head passed among seven households as each preferred a brother and his family, then returned to the first home; the verse was revealed about this.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r1.anchor: Hâkim ve İbn Merdûye ve Şu‘ab’da Beyhakī dahi İbn Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâ Hazretleri’nden şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r2.claim: The cited occasions are only examples; the Ansar and Companions displayed many such acts, including men with two wives giving one up so an unmarried Muhajir could marry.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r2.anchor: Hatta ensardan iki zevcesi bulunanlar zevcesi olmayan muhacirlerin evlenmesi için zevcelerinden birini terk bile etmişlerdi.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r3.claim: At Yarmuk, dying wounded martyrs passed even a sip of water to a groaning companion; Akif's Safahat beautifully depicts the sacred historical episode.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r3.anchor: Yermük vak‘asında şehidler içinde son nefesine gelmiş yaralıların kendilerine verilen bir yudum suyu bile yanında inleyen arkadaşına

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r4.claim: Those protected from the soul's shuhh—greed, envy, and stinginess—are the truly successful, escaping every harm and attaining their aims; this is both an ethical principle and glad tidings for the Ansar and their imitators.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r4.anchor: ahlâkī bir saadet düstûru, hem de ensârın ve onların ahlâklarına imtisal edenlerin medhiyle haklarında bir tebşirdir.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r5.claim: Shuhh is an ingrained disposition of greed, envy, and miserliness; buhl is its practical manifestation in withholding.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r5.anchor: “Şuhh” nefsin bahillik, nekeslik, hasislik dediğimiz hırs ve kıskançlık huyudur

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r6.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r6.claim: Raghib defines shuhh as greed and miserliness that have become habitual.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r6.anchor: Râgıb bunu “âdet hâline gelmiş hırs ile buhl” diye târif etmiştir.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r7.speaker: Hasan
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r7.claim: Hasan distinguishes buhl as begrudging what one owns from shuhh as begrudging what anyone else owns.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r7.anchor: İbn Münzir’in Hasan’dan rivayetine göre “buhl” insanın elindekini kıskanması, “şuhh” da herkesin elindekini kıskanması diye târif edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r8.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masud tells a man who fears his stinginess means doom that this is buhl, not Quranic shuhh; shuhh is unjustly consuming one's brother's property.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r8.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd Hazretleri de “o şuhh değil, buhldur, buhlde de hayır yoktur. Allah teâlâ’nın zikrettiği şuhh ise kardeşinin malını zulmen yemendir” diye cevap vermiştir.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r9.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r9.claim: Ibn Umar says shuhh is not withholding one's own property but coveting what does not belong to oneself.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r9.anchor: İbn Münzir’in ve İbn Merdûye’nin rivayet ettikleri vechile İbn Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâ Hazretleri de demiştir ki

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r10.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r10.claim: Alusi finds no lexicographers' support for those definitions and suggests shuhh is buhl at its extreme: resenting others' generosity, trying to stop it, wrongfully taking their property, or envying what they have.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r10.anchor: Âlûsî bunları naklettikten sonra der ki: “Lügaviyyûnun hiçbirinde ‘şuhh’un bu târiflerinden bir şey görmedim

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r11.claim: The verse condemns shuhh as extremely blameworthy: success is restricted to those protected from it, excluding those who are not protected.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r11.anchor: şuhdan vikāye edilenlere kasredilmiş olmakla ondan vikāye edilmemiş olanlar felah bulanların hâricinde kalmış olur.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r12.speaker: Enes
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r12.claim: A Prophetic report from Anas says nothing destroys Islam as completely as shuhh.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r12.anchor: Hakîm-i Tirmizî ve Ebû Ya‘lâ ve İbn Merdûye Enes radıyallâhu anh’tan merfû‘an rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r13.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r13.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says the dust of God's path and Hell's smoke never coexist in a servant's body, nor faith and shuhh in a heart.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r13.anchor: İbn Ebî Şeybe, Nesâî ve Beyhakī ve Hâkim Ebû Hüreyre radıyallâhu anh’tan merfû‘an rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r14.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r14.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri says stinginess and bad character do not coexist in a Muslim; Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r14.anchor: Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî “garîb” diyerek, Edeb’de Buhârî ve daha diğerleri Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî radıyallâhu anh’tan merfû‘an rivayet eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r15.speaker: Enes
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r15.claim: In a report from Anas, God commands Eden to speak; it says “The believers have succeeded,” and God swears no miser will dwell near Him there. The Prophet then recites 59:9.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r15.anchor: İbn Ebi’d- Dünya ve İbn Adî ve Hâkim ve Hatîb Enes radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r16.speaker: Câbir b. Abdillah
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r16.claim: A Prophetic report from Jabir warns against injustice and shuhh: shuhh destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and treating forbidden things as lawful.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r16.anchor: Ahmed, Edeb’de Buhârî, Müslim, Beyhakī, Câbir b. Abdillah radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r17.claim: Protection from shuhh does not require a person to be generous in every matter.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r17.anchor: şuhdan korunmak bir kişinin her şeyde cömert olmasına mütevakkıf değildir.

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r18.speaker: Mücemmi‘ b. Yahyâ
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r18.claim: A Prophetic report says one is free of shuhh by paying zakat, hosting a guest, and helping during a calamity.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r18.anchor: Mücemmi‘[^36] b. Yahyâ’dan merfû‘an rivayet eylemişlerdir ki:

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r19.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r19.claim: Ali says that whoever pays zakat on his wealth is protected from the shuhh of his soul.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r19.anchor: İbn Münzir de Hazret-i Ali radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle rivayet eylemiştir ki

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r20.speaker: Ebû Heyyâc-ı Esedî
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r20.claim: Abu Hayyaj al-Asadi reports meeting a man at the Kaaba who only prayed for protection from shuhh, explaining that such protection would keep him from theft, adultery, and wrongdoing; the man was Abdurrahman ibn Awf.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r20.anchor: İbn Cerîr Taberî, Ebû Heyyâc-ı Esedî’den rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:59:9#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r21.speaker: İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r21.claim: Ibn Zayd says one is protected from shuhh by neither taking what God forbids nor letting it prevent one from fulfilling what God commands; such a person is successful.
ELMALILI:59:9#2/r21.anchor: İbn Zeyd de demiştir ki: “Bir kimse Allah’ın nehyettiği bir şey için bir şey almaz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r8.speaker: Yaygın görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r8.claim: War-acquired land and its revenues, along with kharaj and jizya, count as fayʾ and are handled under verses 7–10; the beneficiaries include the groups in verse 7, the Emigrants and Helpers, and later Muslims.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r8.anchor: savaş sonucu elde edilen araziler, bunların gelirleri, gayri müslimlerden alınan haraç ve cizye vergileri fey‘ kabul edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r13.speaker: Hz. Ömer
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r13.claim: After Iraq’s conquest, Saʿd relayed the soldiers’ request to distribute the Sawad lands; after consulting the Companions, ʿUmar distributed movable spoils but left land and waterways with their owners as a public endowment, directing kharaj to the treasury for Muslims’ stipends.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r13.anchor: Ömer konuyu sahâbe ile geniş biçimde tartıştıktan sonra menkul malların (ganimet statüsünde olmak üzere) müslüman askerler arasında dağıtılmasına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r23.claim: Read with verses 9–10, verse 8 honors the Emigrants’ singular faith and sacrifice, calls for love and respect for them across generations, and gives their poor priority when Muslims’ resources are shared.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r23.anchor: burada muhacirlerin, eşsiz iman tezahürleri ve unutulmaz özverili davranışlarıyla İslâm tebliğinde tuttuğu özel ve seçkin yere

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r24.claim: The verse praises the Helpers for welcoming the Prophet’s Emigrants, sharing their means joyfully, and preferring them despite their own need; ethicists coined īthār for this special virtue of preferring another to oneself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r24.anchor: Ensarın bu örnek kişiliğinden söz edilirken “ihtiyaç içinde olsalar bile onları kendilerine tercih ederler” ifadesi kullanıldığından

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r26.claim: Verses 8–10 portray the ideal believer and offer formative warnings about faith, selflessness, and care for future generations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r26.anchor: bu üç âyette, ideal mümin tipi ve karakteriyle ilgili tasvirlerin ve eğitici-öğretici uyarıların hakim olduğu görülür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r27.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r27.claim: Believers should credit success to God’s grace and aid rather than their own power, treating confidence as lived faith and trust in its saving power rather than perfection of personal talent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r27.anchor: Bütün hayırlı eylemlerde, başarılı olmak için kendi gücüne değil Allah’ın lutuf ve inayetine olan inancı öne çıkarmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r28.claim: They should make earning God’s pleasure their aim and interpret all their conduct by that principle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r28.anchor: Allah’ın hoşnutluğunu kazanmayı amaç edinmek, bütün davranışlarını bu ilkeye göre anlamlandırmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r29.claim: They should help God’s Messenger by being willing to sacrifice their most valued worldly desires and interests for proclaiming God’s commands and prohibitions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r29.anchor: Allah’a ve resulüne yardım yani Allah’ın buyruk ve yasaklarını tebliğ uğruna gerektiğinde en değerli dünyevî arzu ve çıkarlarını feda edebilmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r30.claim: The ideal believer does not compromise honesty and remains faithful to their word.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r30.anchor: Dürüstlükten ödün vermemek, söze sadakat göstermek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r31.claim: They should welcome a needy fellow believer and share from a basis of love, guarding sincerity against selfish impulses, affectation, and showing off.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r31.anchor: Darda olan mümin kardeşine kucak açmak; ama imkânlarını onunla paylaşırken ve onun için özveride bulunurken bunun sevgi temeline dayalı kalmasına özen göstermek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r32.claim: They should continually seek God’s help and protection against human weaknesses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r32.anchor: Beşerî zaaflara karşı daima Allah’ın yardımına ve korumasına sığınmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r33.claim: They should trust in God’s encompassing mercy, pray for fellow believers’ forgiveness, and remember their own human fallibility when they notice others’ faults.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r33.anchor: Allah’ın şefkat ve merhametinin herkesi kuşatacak enginlikte olduğuna yürekten inanmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r34.speaker: Yaygın yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r34.claim: Tebevvee can mean taking up residence or preparing; most interpreters take the first sense, yielding a literal “settled in the abode and faith” that requires supplying an unexpressed verb before “faith” to mean sincere belief, as in the translation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r34.anchor: Genellikle âyet bu fiilin ilk anlamına göre yorumlanmakta, bu durumda ibarenin lafzî karşılığı “onlardan önce bu yurda ve imana yerleşmiş olanlar” şeklinde olmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r35.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r35.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r35.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya takes the conjunction between “abode” and “faith” as expressing accompaniment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r35.anchor: İbn Atıyye ise “dâr” ile “iman” kelimeleri arasındaki “ve” bağlacının “beraberlik” anlamında düşünülebileceği kanaatindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r36.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r36.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r36.claim: Ibn ʿAshur calls the accompaniment reading best, despite not having many adherents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r36.anchor: İbn Âşûr –fazla taraftarı olmamakla beraber– en iyi yorumun bu olduğunu söyler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r37.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r37.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r37.claim: Elmalili approves the accompaniment reading because it avoids positing words absent from the text.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r37.anchor: Elmalılı da, böylece metinde yer almayan bazı lafızları var saymaya gerek kalmayacağını belirterek bu yorumu güzel bulur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r38.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r38.claim: The author favors taking tebevvee as “prepare,” translating the phrase as those who prepared the abode through faith; this avoids the historically false implication that the Helpers acquired their land through faith or acquired the land and faith together.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r38.anchor: Bizce de bu yaklaşım yerinde olmakla birlikte, bu takdirde anılan fiilin “hazırlama” mânasını esas alıp âyetin belirtilen kısmını “onlardan önce imanla bu yurdu hazırlamış olanlar” şeklinde çevirmek uygun olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r39.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r39.speaker: Birçok müfessir
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r39.claim: Many commentators define shuh as extreme miserliness, or as miserliness combined with envy of what others possess.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r39.anchor: Birçok müfessire göre bu kelime “cimrilik huyunun ileri derecesi” veya “cimri olmanın yanı sıra başkalarının elindeki imkânları da kıskanma” anlamına gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r40.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r40.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r40.claim: Drawing especially on al-Zamakhshari, the author renders the phrase as succeeding in guarding oneself from selfishness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r40.anchor: Biz özellikle Zemahşerî’nin açıklamasından yararlanarak âyetin ilgili kısmını, “Kim nefsinin bencilliğinden korunmayı başarırsa” diye çevirdik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r41.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r41.speaker: Birçok müfessir
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r41.claim: Another common interpretation is resistance to personal desire in obeying God: avoiding prohibitions and unlawful food, fulfilling commands, and enjoying what is lawful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r41.anchor: Birçok müfessire göre de bu kısım “Allah’ın yasakladıklarından uzak durma, haram yememe, buyruklarını yerine getirme ve helalden yararlanma konusunda nefsine yenilmeyen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r42.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r42.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r42.claim: Al-Razi defines shuh as the psychological state that drives a person toward miserliness, allowing the phrase to be translated as protection from miserly feeling.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:6/r42.anchor: Râzî, bunu “cimriliğe iten hâlet-i ruhiye” diye açıklar ki buna göre âyetin bu kısmını “kim cimrilik duygusundan korunursa” şeklinde tercüme etmek mümkündür

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r1.speaker: أبو المتوكل الناجي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r1.claim: Abū al-Mutawakkil al-Nājī gives a similar report, specifying that the man who hosted Thābit b. Qays b. Shammās was the one concerned by this verse.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r1.anchor: وأخرج مسدد في مسنده وابن المنذر عن أبي المتوكل الناجي ان رجلا من المسلمين فذكر نحوه وفيه أن الرجل الذي أضاف ثابت بن قيس

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that a Companion passed a gifted sheep's head to a needier brother; it circulated through seven households before returning to the first, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p209/r2.anchor: وأخرج الواحدي من طريق محارب بن دثار عن ابن عمر قال أهدي لرجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأس شاة فقال إن أخي فلانا وعياله أحوج إلى هذا منا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r3.speaker: يزيد بن الأصم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r3.claim: Yazid ibn al-Asamm reports that the Ansar offered to divide their land equally with the emigrants; the Prophet declined, proposing that they share the produce while the land stayed theirs, and the verse was revealed after they agreed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r3.anchor: روى جعفر بن برقان عن يزيد بن الأصم: أن الأنصار قالوا: يا رسول الله، اقسم بيننا وبين إخواننا من المهاجرين

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that an Ansari family served its only meal to an Ahl al-Suffa guest while concealing their own hunger; the Prophet said heaven marveled at their deed, and the verse was revealed. Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - دفع إلى رجل من الأنصار رجلا من أهل الصفة،

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports that a sheep's head passed among seven households, each sending it onward because another family was needier, until it returned to the first; the verse was revealed about this selflessness.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p419/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: أهدي لرجل من أصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - رأس شاة، فقال: إن أخي فلانا وعياله أحوج إلى هذا منا

DAMGHANI:v1p112/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p112/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p112/r7.claim: Ḥubb can mean preferring or giving priority to others; the Anṣār prefer those who emigrated to them.
DAMGHANI:v1p112/r7.anchor: فوجه منها الحب والاستحباب الإيثار قوله تعالى في سورة ص

BURHAN:v3p123/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p123/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p123/r5.claim: One verb is shared by two objects though a second fitting verb is implicit: they settled in Medina and believed in faith.
BURHAN:v3p123/r5.anchor: الرابع أن يستدل بالفعل لشيئين وهو في الحقيقة لأحدهما فيضمر للآخر فعل يناسبه
